No model output was implantable because predictions failed to both avoid existing bone and add useful material.
A task-specific volumetric model was implantable on all but one case, indicating the limitation is not inherent to the task.
At the tested point densities, emitted points cannot reliably determine implant thickness, highlighting a representation-level limitation.
papers.selection_reason: Audits pretrained 3D shape completion foundation models for cranial defect reconstruction; directly addresses trustworthiness and usability of 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Plausible but Unimplantable: A Trustworthiness Audit of Shape Completion Foundation Models for Cranial Defect Reconstruction
papers.tldr: An audit finds that publicly released shape-completion foundation models produce plausible-looking but clinically unimplantable cranial reconstructions in zero-shot use.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward visual geometry models, exemplified by VGGT, have demonstrated strong multi-view reconstruction capabilities through dense global attention. However, the resulting all-to-all cross-view computation scales quadratically with the number of input views, making long-sequence inference particularly expensive due to substantial frame-level redundancy among highly overlapping observations. We uncover a topology-first, geometry-later evolution in VGGT camera tokens: shallow-layer tokens reliably capture local view neighborhoods, whereas deeper-layer tokens progressively encode globally organized inter-view geometry. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for structure-aware frame-level key--value sparsification. At each global-attention block, BlazeVGGT constructs a view-level similarity kernel from camera-token relations and employs greedy determinantal point process inference to select a compact set of mutually complementary views. The selected views constitute the key--value context, while all input frames are retained as queries. This asymmetric attention design preserves dense per-frame predictions while eliminating redundant cross-view computation, allowing our method to be directly integrated into pretrained VGGT as a plug-and-play module without parameter updates. Its advantages become increasingly pronounced with sequence length: at 2,000 frames, BlazeVGGT achieves approximately 13$\times$ faster inference than VGGT while reducing the Chamfer Distance from 0.41 to 0.32. Extensive experiments demonstrate a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off in point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation, compatibility with existing VGGT accelerators such as FastVGGT and LiteVGGT, and transferability to VGGT-based models including StreamVGGT and PAGE-4D. Codes are publicly available at https://github.com/MagiciannnY/BlazeVGGT.git.
authors: Shujun Yao, Junhui Lin, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Ziwen Liu, Bonan Li
bullets: VGGT’s all-to-all attention becomes costly for long, highly overlapping image sequences.
The method uses camera-token similarities to identify local-to-global view structure across network layers.
Greedy determinantal point process selection chooses complementary frames as sparse key–value context, while retaining all frames as queries.
At 2,000 frames, inference is approximately 13× faster and Chamfer Distance decreases from 0.41 to 0.32.
The plug-and-play approach transfers to VGGT variants and supports point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for sparsifying camera tokens in multi-view geometry models, fitting 3D Vision and Efficient AI.
papers.title: BlazeVGGT: 13x Faster VGGT at 2,000 Frames via Camera Token without Training
papers.tldr: BlazeVGGT makes VGGT about 13× faster on 2,000-frame sequences by sparsifying redundant cross-view attention without retraining, while improving reported reconstruction accuracy.

papers.abstract: Robots deployed in human-centered environments need maps that support both geometric navigation and open-vocabulary semantic queries beyond a fixed label set. A key challenge is enriching such maps with semantic information without relying on manually annotated segmentation masks or closed-set semantic categories. Existing geometry-driven active mapping maximizes coverage but treats semantics as a passive by-product of the collected trajectory, whereas active semantic mapping typically depends on supervised semantic segmentation. We present AOV-GS, an active 3D Gaussian mapping system that guides exploration using frozen foundation models. During coarse exploration, AOV-GS re-ranks geometrically promising candidate views according to CLIP mask-embedding novelty computed from SAM instance segmentation, biasing exploration toward semantically informative regions. Frozen SAM and CLIP provide instance masks and language-aligned embeddings throughout mapping, while a lightweight scene-specific language field is fitted offline directly to the collected CLIP embeddings rather than manually annotated masks, enabling open-vocabulary text-query segmentation on novel views. In a controlled comparison using the same SAM-CLIP perception stack, AOV-GS improves average language-field mIoU over geometry-only active planning by 1.3 percentage points on Replica (34.6% on eight scenes) and by 1.8 points on Matterport3D (23.1% on five scenes). With CorrCLIP, AOV-GS reaches 35.6% on Replica, 2.0 points above the matched Geometry-based + CorrCLIP baseline. Novel-view PSNR remains comparable to the geometry-only baseline on both datasets while depth L1 improves on Replica. Code is available at https://github.com/OptimusFaber/AOV-GS.
authors: Rodion Shkokov, Tatiana Zemskova, Dmitry Yudin
bullets: Targets robot maps that support both geometric navigation and language-based semantic queries beyond fixed label sets.
Re-ranks candidate views using CLIP embedding novelty from SAM instance masks, complementing geometry-driven exploration.
Fits a lightweight scene-specific language field directly to frozen SAM-CLIP embeddings for text-query segmentation on novel views.
Improves language-field mIoU over matched geometry-only planning by 1.3 points on Replica and 1.8 points on Matterport3D.
Maintains comparable novel-view PSNR and improves depth L1 on Replica; evaluation covers eight Replica and five Matterport3D scenes.
papers.selection_reason: Active open-vocabulary semantic mapping using 3D Gaussian Splatting, directly relevant to embodied AI navigation and 3D foundation models.
papers.title: AOV-GS: Active Open-Vocabulary Semantic Mapping with 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.tldr: AOV-GS actively explores environments for semantically informative views, enabling open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian maps without manual segmentation annotations.

papers.abstract: One-shot landmark localization in volume scans with varying fields of view (FOVs) is challenging. While existing self-supervised learning methods have shown promising performance, they rely on contrastive learning built upon augmented views of the same image, which inherently limits their generalization in cross-modality scenarios. This motivates research on cross-modality embedding learning using paired multi-modality images. However, existing methods suffer from not only limited training data, but also the requirement of multi-stage iterative training. To address these limitations, we propose UNIVERS, an end-to-end trainable framework that learns UNIversal Voxel-wise Embedding via Randomized Synthesis. Our framework leverages diverse pseudo-data synthesized from organ shape templates, with randomization applied to semantic layout, visual appearance, FOV, and spatial pose. Coupled with cross-domain discriminative voxel-wise contrastive learning, this domain randomization strategy forces the network to disregard domain-specific biases and learn features that are robust against variations in imaging contrast, resolution, and spatial context. Consequently, the trained model enables one-shot landmark localization in multi-modality volume scans with arbitrary FOVs. In this study, the efficacy of the proposed method is demonstrated by applying it to the task of localizing the adrenal glands, which are paired, small, and irregular endocrine organs. In particular, comprehensive experiments are conducted on three challenging adrenal gland datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that UNIVERS consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art (SOTA) one-shot landmark localization approaches, with particularly prominent advantages in cross-modality scenarios. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Kendra9999/UNIVERS.
authors: Derong Yu, Qingsong Zhao, Yanbing Yue, Yikai Li, Zhi Zhang, Guoyan Zheng
bullets: Targets cross-modality one-shot landmark localization in volume scans with varying or arbitrary FOVs.
Uses an end-to-end framework combining randomized synthesis of pseudo-data with cross-domain discriminative voxel-wise contrastive learning.
Randomizes organ layouts, appearance, FOV, and pose to reduce domain-specific biases and improve robustness to contrast, resolution, and spatial-context changes.
Evaluated on adrenal-gland localization across three challenging datasets, where it consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, especially across modalities.
Scope demonstrated on paired, small, irregular adrenal glands; source code is publicly available.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces UNIVERS, a framework for learning generalizable voxel-wise embeddings in 3D medical scans via randomized synthesis and cross-domain contrastive learning.
papers.title: UNIVERS: Learning UNIversal Voxel-wise Embedding via Randomized Synthesis for generalizable one-shot landmark localization
papers.tldr: UNIVERS enables robust one-shot landmark localization across modalities and arbitrary fields of view by learning voxel embeddings from heavily randomized synthetic data.

papers.abstract: Abdominal organ segmentation is essential in modern medical applications. While existing deep learning approaches demonstrate promising performance, their heavy reliance on large-scale image data raises concerns over generalization capability and privacy risks. This motivates the development of generalizable segmentation training paradigms based on domain-randomized image synthesis, facilitating generalization across unseen real image domains. However, existing paradigms either suffer from limited segmentation performance when applied to abdominal organs, or require dataset-specific finetuning. To address these limitations, we propose ReSeg, a novel two-stage retraining-free framework for domain-agnostic zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation. At the first stage, our organ-agnostic synthetic data-driven pretraining approach exploits semantically and visually diverse synthetic images generated by a dedicated data engine to optimize a Generalizable Semantic Representation Network (GSRNet). The network is thereby capable of learning semantic features robust against variations in anatomical structure, imaging contrast, resolution and spatial context, which provide universal representation capabilities that serve as a foundation for segmentation learning. Subsequently, in the second stage, we continue to train an Organ-specific Encoder-decoder Segmentation Network (OESNet), whose encoder is initialized with the pretrained weights. This training process is facilitated by another dedicated data engine, which generates diversified visual images while strictly retaining the inherent spatial layout of abdominal organs. Comprehensive evaluation on seven abdominal organ segmentation datasets across three different modalities including CT, MRI, and PET demonstrates that ReSeg consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods while eliminating the need for real training images.
bullets: Addresses limited cross-domain generalization, privacy concerns, and the need for dataset-specific fine-tuning in abdominal organ segmentation.
Uses a two-stage framework: organ-agnostic synthetic pretraining of GSRNet, followed by organ-specific OESNet training initialized from the learned encoder.
Employs dedicated data engines to generate visually diverse synthetic images while preserving organ layouts and semantic structure.
Learns representations robust to anatomical, contrast, resolution, and spatial-context variations.
Evaluation across seven datasets and three imaging modalities shows consistent improvement over existing state-of-the-art methods without real training images.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a generalizable pretraining framework (ReSeg) for 3D medical image segmentation using domain-randomized synthesis and semantic representation learning.
papers.title: ReSeg: Retraining-free segmentation of abdominal organs via generalizable semantic representation learning
papers.tldr: ReSeg enables retraining-free, zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation across unseen CT, MRI, and PET domains using synthetic-data-driven semantic representation learning.

papers.abstract: We present Register Anything Model (RAM), a unified model for generalizable 3D point cloud registration that robustly estimates 6-DoF transformations across diverse domains spanning sensors and environments. Existing registration methods are typically tailored to a single domain, with carefully tuned architectures and hyperparameters, and thus degrade markedly when applied to novel domains. We bridge this gap by training a single model on diverse data from indoor, outdoor, and object domains. A central challenge is the severe geometric discrepancy across domains, i.e., differences in scene scale, sensor noise, point density, and structural patterns, which hinders processing with a unified point-based model. To address this, we introduce a geometry-aware normalization strategy that jointly voxelizes and normalizes point clouds into a standardized geometric space, adaptively based on their geometric properties to preserve salient local structures while standardizing resolution. Built on this normalization, RAM follows a hierarchical coarse-to-fine paradigm, and employs an efficient geometric transformer that models local geometric consistency instead of globally over all points. This design mitigates discretization noise introduced by voxelization, and improves computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on 12 benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in terms of inlier ratio and registration recall. Notably, our method outperforms the counterparts trained on each separate domain, showing superior generalization capability.
authors: Zheng Qin, Junhua Xi, Yan Huang, Jiahong Lai, Anwen Huang, Qiong Li, Guangda Zhang, Kai Xu
bullets: Targets the poor cross-domain generalization of registration methods tuned to individual sensors or environments.
Jointly voxelizes and normalizes point clouds according to their geometry, standardizing resolution while preserving salient local structures.
Uses a hierarchical coarse-to-fine pipeline with a local geometric transformer for efficient geometric-consistency modeling.
Trained on diverse indoor, outdoor, and object data, RAM achieves state-of-the-art inlier ratio and registration recall across 12 benchmarks.
Outperforms models trained separately for each domain, demonstrating stronger generalization across domains.
papers.selection_reason: Unified generalizable 3D point cloud registration across domains fits 3D vision and generalist 3D modeling.
papers.title: Register Anything Model for Generalizable and Robust Point Cloud Registration
papers.tldr: RAM is a unified point-cloud registration model that uses geometry-aware normalization and efficient hierarchical matching to generalize robustly across diverse 3D domains.

papers.abstract: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.
authors: Noam Rotstein, Yoad Tewel, Chen Tessler, Haggai Maron, Gal Chechik, Or Litany, Yoni Kasten, Yuval Atzmon
bullets: Addresses the gap between realistic video generation and usable 3D animation for specific assets.
Separates an arbitrary-skeleton 3D motion model from a pretrained video model, linking them with lightweight cross-attention.
Predicts joint locations in video to recover the camera and register 3D motion in the scene.
Uses curated synthetic edits plus human and robot video to create nearly 200K training pairs.
Supports text-to-motion/video, video-to-rig motion, rig-motion-to-video, and keyframe control; evaluations report more faithful, scene-responsive animation than video-first pipelines.
papers.selection_reason: Co-generates 3D motion and video for arbitrary rigs from human/robot video; transferable to embodied animation and 3D motion generation.
papers.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
papers.tldr: Joints, Camera, Action! co-generates scene-aware video, camera motion, and replayable 3D motion for arbitrary rigs from text or video.

papers.abstract: Simulation is a powerful tool for robotics, but building diverse, simulation-ready scenes at scale remains difficult. Reconstructing scenes from single images is a promising alternative, but visual similarity alone is insufficient: objects must also be recovered, accurately placed, and physically grounded. Existing methods that rely on post-hoc physics settling often misplace objects, producing scenes that look correct but behave poorly under manipulation. We present SceneRig, an agentic system that turns a single image into an editable, simulation-ready scene. SceneRig combines geometric, visual, and physical tools to reconstruct a faithful 3D scene. An agent then performs edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to achieve physical stability. Across diverse inputs, SceneRig improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement while keeping the reconstructed scenes physically stable. Furthermore, SceneRig is effective for downstream robotics: its scenes predict real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than the baseline method and more reliably support replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.
authors: Rundong Luo, Yunong Liu, Di Cao, Matthew Tancik, Shyamal Buch, Colton Stearns, Wenqi Xian
bullets: Addresses the gap between visually plausible reconstruction and physically correct object placement.
Combines geometric, visual, and physical tools with agent-driven edit-and-validate loops in a physics simulator.
Improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement across diverse inputs.
Produces physically stable scenes that better predict real-robot policy outcomes than the baseline.
Supports more reliable replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.
papers.selection_reason: Agentic system for 3D scene reconstruction from single images with physical grounding, directly applicable to simulation and downstream robotics tasks.
papers.title: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
papers.tldr: SceneRig reconstructs editable, physically stable 3D scenes from single images for more reliable simulation and robot-policy evaluation.

papers.abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonstrate improved final accuracy and faster convergence compared to random initialization. Additionally, its frozen embeddings outperform anatomically defined volumetric features on four of five downstream classification tasks and perform competitively with a state-of-the-art foundation model pre-trained on substantially more data. Lastly, we show that Brain2Vec encodes information primarily from a spatially localized and neuroanatomically meaningful set of brain regions, and that manipulating a subset of latent features produces monotonic, region-specific effects on the reconstructed anatomy. Brain2Vec code and trained models are available as an open-source package on https://github.com/CBICA/Brain2Vec. Users can apply Brain2Vec locally by installing the package, or directly through the NiChart cloud platform https://cloud.neuroimagingchart.com, where Brain2Vec features can be derived without requiring local installation or specialized infrastructure.
authors: Spiros Maggioros, Guray Erus, Gareth Harman, George Aidinis, Alexander Getka, Aristeidis Sotiras, Christos Davatzikos
bullets: Pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted MRI scans pooled from multiple studies.
Supports both weight initialization for downstream fine-tuning and standalone feature extraction.
Improved brain-age prediction accuracy and convergence speed relative to random initialization.
Frozen embeddings outperformed anatomical volumetric features on four of five classification tasks and competed with a larger-data foundation model.
Latent features capture spatially localized, neuroanatomically meaningful information with region-specific effects on reconstructed anatomy.
papers.selection_reason: Self-supervised 3D foundation model for brain MRI; fits 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
papers.tldr: Brain2Vec is a self-supervised 3D foundation model for structural brain MRI that improves fine-tuning efficiency and provides informative, neuroanatomically meaningful embeddings.

papers.abstract: Existing feature lifting approaches for open-vocabulary segmentation rely on simple backprojection to assign features to primitives. In the case of 3D Gaussian splatting reconstruction, the primitives overlap heavily, leading to suboptimal reconstructions, governed by many primitives per ray. Backprojection, however, reduces to a least-squares solvable problem, exactly when no two primitives share a ray. Motivated by this insight, we propose OV-Foam, which uses PowerFoam as the underlying representation. This representation uses a power-diagram to partition the scene, resulting in zero overlap between primitives and a substantial reduction in primitives per ray, which ultimately simplifies the lifting problem and allows for closer-to-optimal feature assignment. We show that the space partitioning primitives of OV-Foam reach near-optimal assignment, and our experiments demonstrate improved open-vocabulary segmentation over Gaussian baselines.
authors: Yousef Rajeh (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology), Alejandra Esparza Pelcastre (Universidad Panamericana), Ivan Viola (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology), Dominik Engel (King Abdullah University of Science and Technology)
bullets: Existing methods use backprojection, but overlapping Gaussian primitives make feature assignment difficult.
OV-Foam uses PowerFoam to partition scenes into non-overlapping primitives.
Fewer primitives per ray simplify lifting and bring it closer to the least-squares optimum.
The representation achieves near-optimal feature assignment and improves open-vocabulary segmentation over Gaussian baselines.
papers.selection_reason: Improves open-vocabulary segmentation using 3D Gaussian Splatting with a PowerFoam representation to reduce overlap and optimize feature lifting. Fits 3D Foundation Models and Spatial Intelligence.
papers.title: OV-Foam: How 3D Representations Shape Semantic Feature Lifting
papers.tldr: OV-Foam improves open-vocabulary 3D feature lifting by replacing overlapping Gaussian primitives with non-overlapping power-diagram cells for more accurate feature assignment.

papers.abstract: Examining existing benchmarks for grounding in 3D VLMs reveals a pervasive "semantic leakage" in the evaluation and prompting protocols: a heavy reliance on bounding boxes as spatial prompts or representation primitives. Because bounding boxes are highly informative of object categories, they introduce a shortcut for the models to neglect visual information during 3D VLM training. We demonstrate this with a "blind" LLM that, prompted only with the box coordinates, can perform surprisingly well. To further analyze this shortcut, we propose point-based grounding prompting - querying models with a single 3D point instead of a box. Under this protocol, the accuracy of the blind LLM drops from 36.4% to 18.0% on ScanNet's Nr3D, and similarly degrades for 3D VLMs (e.g. LL3DA). Building on this insight, we introduce P$^3$-VLM, a novel tri-pathway 3D VLM that supports point-based prompts and achieves 52.1% state-of-the-art accuracy on location-grounded captioning under this setting. To achieve this, we redesign the architecture while keeping it detector-free, scene-centric, and suitable for 3D GS inputs. P$^3$-VLM utilizes three complementary pathways (location-, task-, and context-aware), enabling strong reasoning about scenes without any bounding box dependencies. The key benefit of point-based learning is a consistent improvement across settings: P$^3$-VLM achieves state-of-the-art performance under point-based grounding while also improving robustness, OOD generalization, and performance on ungrounded scene-centric 3D VQA benchmarks, reflecting its reduced reliance on bounding-box shortcuts and resulting stronger visual-spatial reasoning.
authors: Anna-Maria Halacheva, Jan-Nico Zaech, Sombit Dey, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel
bullets: Existing 3D VLM grounding benchmarks risk semantic leakage because bounding boxes reveal object-category information.
A blind LLM using only box coordinates reaches 36.4% on ScanNet Nr3D, but falls to 18.0% with a single 3D point, exposing the shortcut.
P$^3$-VLM is a detector-free, scene-centric, tri-pathway 3D VLM designed for point prompts and 3D Gaussian Splatting inputs.
Its location-, task-, and context-aware pathways achieve 52.1% accuracy on point-based location-grounded captioning.
Point-based learning also improves robustness, out-of-distribution generalization, and ungrounded scene-centric 3D VQA performance.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes P$^3$-VLM, a 3D VLM that uses point-based grounding to mitigate semantic leakage in bounding boxes, improving visual-spatial reasoning and robustness. Fits Spatial Intelligence (geometry-aware VLM) and 3D Foundation Models.
papers.title: P$^3$-VLM: A Point-based Alternative for Grounded 3D Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: P$^3$-VLM replaces shortcut-prone 3D bounding-box prompts with point-based grounding and achieves stronger visual-spatial reasoning without box dependencies.

papers.abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) achieve high-quality novel-view synthesis by representing a scene as a continuous volumetric radiance field. However, the geometry encoded by the density field of vanilla NeRF can be noisy and inaccurate, since different combinations of shape and radiance may explain the same input images. To reduce this ambiguity, we augment vanilla NeRF with a geometry-optimization branch based on self-supervised cross-ray consistency. Specifically, this branch samples candidate surface points from the density field, generates virtual rays that intersect at each point from different directions, and renders their appearance using the NeRF network. Based on the visibility-weighted color consistency across these rays, we constrain the implicit geometry. We further regularize the implicit geometry by penalizing opacity at candidates with inconsistent appearance predictions and encouraging local normal smoothness. These geometric constraints are derived from the NeRF predictions and require no ground-truth depth or surface-normal supervision. Experiments on eight Replica scenes show that the proposed method reduces the mean Chamfer distance by 30.8% compared with vanilla NeRF.
bullets: Vanilla NeRF geometry can be noisy because shape and radiance ambiguities explain the same images.
The method samples candidate surfaces from density and evaluates appearance consistency along virtual rays from multiple directions.
Visibility-weighted color consistency constrains geometry without ground-truth depth or normal labels.
Additional regularization penalizes opacity for inconsistent predictions and promotes local normal smoothness.
On eight Replica scenes, mean Chamfer distance decreases by 30.8% versus vanilla NeRF.
papers.selection_reason: Improves NeRF geometry via self-supervised cross-ray consistency, contributing to 3D scene reconstruction and world model representations.
papers.title: Geometry Regularization for Vanilla NeRF via Self-Supervised Cross-Ray Consistency
papers.tldr: A self-supervised cross-ray consistency branch regularizes vanilla NeRF geometry, reducing reconstruction ambiguity and mean Chamfer distance on eight Replica scenes.

papers.abstract: 3D Human Pose Estimation (3D HPE) is used in indoor environments, such as smart homes, to analyze human movement and monitor human states. Millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar is suitable for this task because it is robust to lighting variations and does not capture images of human appearance. However, radar observations often provide insufficient information about certain body parts or contain overlapping reflections from multiple body parts, limiting accurate 3D joint localization. To address these limitations, we propose the Initialization-to-Refinement Pose Framework (I2R-Pose), comprising two stages: Motion-Aware Pose Initialization and Observation-Guided Refinement. In the first stage, joint-wise features are learned by incorporating temporal relationships across consecutive radar observations and human skeletal structure to compensate for insufficient joint information and estimate an initial 3D pose sequence. In the second stage, separately extracted radar observation features predict joint-wise positional corrections that refine the initial pose and generate the final pose sequence. The framework supports individual and fused inputs of time-Doppler/time-range (TD/TR) maps and radar point clouds (PCs). To evaluate performance across indoor activities, we construct the Radar Motion and Spatial Information for 3D Human Pose Estimation (RaMoS-Pose) dataset, providing synchronized TD/TR maps, radar PCs, and 3D joint ground truth (GT). Evaluations on RaMoS-Pose and the publicly available MVDoppler-Pose dataset show that I2R-Pose reduces mean per-joint position error (MPJPE) by 39.50% on MVDoppler-Pose and by 15.13% on RaMoS-Pose with fused inputs, compared with the best-performing existing methods evaluated on each dataset.
authors: Woo-Jin Jung, Chan-Bin Lim, Seung-Hyun Kong
bullets: Addresses missing or overlapping mmWave radar reflections that hinder accurate 3D joint localization.
Uses a two-stage pipeline: motion-aware pose initialization followed by observation-guided joint correction.
Supports TD/TR maps, radar point clouds, and their fusion.
Introduces the RaMoS-Pose dataset with synchronized radar data and 3D joint ground truth.
With fused inputs, reduces MPJPE by 39.50% on MVDoppler-Pose and 15.13% on RaMoS-Pose versus the best evaluated existing methods.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a radar-based 3D human pose estimation framework (I2R-Pose) for indoor environments. This contributes to 3D perception (3D Vision) and provides a sensor modality for embodied agents.
papers.title: Radar-Based 3D Human Pose Estimation via Motion-Aware Pose Initialization and Observation-Guided Refinement
papers.tldr: I2R-Pose improves radar-based 3D human pose estimation by initializing poses from motion and skeletal context, then refining them with radar observations.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (FF3DGS) reconstructs 3D scenes from images in a single forward pass, making it well-suited to applications that must operate within limited resource budgets. To further improve its practicality, recent budget-controllable FF3DGS methods allow the number of Gaussians to be adjusted at inference, so that the output meets a given storage limit or rendering-latency constraint. However, these methods overlook the cost of inference itself: to produce a representation with the target number of Gaussians, they first predict a dense set of Gaussians and then prune or select from it, requiring nearly constant latency and peak memory regardless of the budget. We therefore propose RLSplat, a resource-linear budget-controllable FF3DGS framework whose representation size, inference latency, and peak memory all decrease linearly as the Gaussian budget is reduced. Instead of pruning or selection, RLSplat learns a Gaussian allocation policy that distributes the budget across local scene regions, so that exactly the requested number of Gaussians is generated. These Gaussians are then refined through resource-linear Gaussian decoding, in which each Gaussian attends only to nearby Gaussians found via an efficient hierarchical neighbor search, so that the decoding cost decreases linearly with fewer Gaussians. In zero-shot evaluation, RLSplat outperforms prior budget-controllable methods at every budget, surpassing the strongest baseline even with 4$\times$ fewer Gaussians, while running up to 4.1$\times$ faster with 9.6$\times$ less peak memory at low budgets.
authors: Injae Kim, Minseok Joo, Jihwan Park, Sehyung Kim, Minseong Bae, Hyunwoo J. Kim
bullets: Existing methods generate a dense Gaussian set before pruning, so inference cost remains nearly fixed regardless of the final budget.
RLSplat learns how to allocate exactly the requested number of Gaussians across local scene regions.
A resource-linear decoder refines Gaussians using efficient hierarchical neighbor search and local attention.
In zero-shot evaluation, it outperforms prior budget-controllable methods at every budget, including a stronger baseline with 4× fewer Gaussians.
At low budgets, RLSplat runs up to 4.1× faster and uses 9.6× less peak memory.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes RLSplat, a resource-linear budget control method for 3D Gaussian Splatting. This addresses efficiency in 3D foundation models and falls under token/pruning strategies for resource management.
papers.title: RLSplat: Resource-Linear Budget Control for Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.tldr: RLSplat makes feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting truly budget-controllable by reducing representation size, inference latency, and peak memory linearly with the requested Gaussian budget.

papers.abstract: Semantic occupancy mapping supports embodied perception during exploration and detailed scene understanding afterward, giving rise to two complementary requirements: online incremental mapping for maintaining an up-to-date global map under causal constraints, and offline global map refinement for improving the completed scene representation with additional computation. We present VEOcc++, a unified voxel-centric framework that connects both stages through a persistent sparse voxel feature map. During exploration, the map expands with newly observed regions and integrates aligned local features through reliability-guided updates, while context-aware decoding produces the current semantic occupancy map. After exploration, cached local features are consolidated as complementary evidence and combined with the completed online representation for multi-scale spatial refinement. On EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet, VEOcc++ achieves 67.12\% IoU and 58.40\% mIoU, establishing new state-of-the-art performance for online incremental mapping. With the local predictor fixed, our online mapping pipeline outperforms VEOcc fusion by 3.70 IoU and 3.74 mIoU points, demonstrating substantial gains from the proposed global mapping design. Offline global map refinement further improves the completed map to 67.79% IoU and 59.37% mIoU using only the observations acquired during exploration. Zero-shot deployment on a mobile robot further demonstrates transferability to unseen environments, onboard feasibility, and scalability to large-scale indoor mapping. Project page: https://wryzju.github.io/VEOccpp/.
authors: Ruoyu Wang, Jiahan Li, Yong Liu, Kexin Zhang
bullets: Addresses the need for both up-to-date online maps during exploration and more detailed offline reconstruction afterward.
Maintains a persistent voxel-centric map that expands with new regions and integrates local features using reliability-guided updates.
Uses context-aware decoding online, then consolidates cached features for multi-scale offline refinement.
On EmbodiedOcc-ScanNet, achieves 67.12% IoU and 58.40% mIoU online, with offline refinement improving performance to 67.79% IoU and 59.37% mIoU.
Demonstrates transfer to unseen environments, onboard feasibility, and scalable indoor mapping on a mobile robot.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a persistent voxel feature map for online and offline semantic occupancy mapping, a core component for embodied navigation and scene understanding.
papers.title: VEOcc++: Learning Persistent Voxel Feature Maps for Embodied Online Semantic Occupancy Mapping and Offline Refinement
papers.tldr: VEOcc++ uses a persistent sparse voxel feature map to unify causal online semantic occupancy mapping with offline refinement, achieving strong performance and zero-shot mobile-robot transfer.

papers.abstract: 3D scene graphs support language-guided navigation by organizing physical entities and their containment and spatial relations into hierarchical maps. Building such structured maps requires a scene representation that consistently distinguishes semantic regions and object instances across viewpoints. To this end, we present PanoGraphGS, a unified framework that integrates panoptic 3D Gaussian representation learning with hierarchical 3D scene graph construction. The framework learns semantic and instance features on shared Gaussian geometry. Prototype-based semantic learning and association-based instance learning produce consistent panoptic predictions across viewpoints. The learned representation supports novel-view panoptic segmentation and direct Gaussian-level panoptic decoding. A semantic-aware scene graph module further recovers a floor-room-stuff-object hierarchy with containment and spatial relations. We further release NaviGS, a real-world dataset for panoramic scene understanding. The dataset provides 3DGS, mesh, RGB, semantic, and depth data. For 3D scene graph identification, PanoGraphGS outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline in object-node accuracy by more than 50\% points on average across Replica and NaviGS. PanoGraphGS also achieves state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods in 2D panoptic segmentation. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of PanoGraphGS in both hierarchical 3D scene understanding and 2D panoptic segmentation. The project website is available at: https://github.com/gaojh0333/PanoGraphGS.
authors: Jinghan Gao, Siyu Wang, Dongyu Feng, Yiyuan Pan, Rong Xiong
bullets: Uses shared Gaussian geometry with prototype-based semantic learning and association-based instance learning to maintain consistent panoptic predictions across viewpoints.
Supports novel-view panoptic segmentation and direct Gaussian-level panoptic decoding.
Builds floor–room–stuff–object hierarchies with containment and spatial relations through a semantic-aware scene graph module.
Introduces NaviGS, a real-world panoramic scene-understanding dataset containing 3DGS, mesh, RGB, semantic, and depth data.

Outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by over 50 percentage points in average object-node accuracy across Replica and NaviGS, while achieving state-of-the-art 2D panoptic segmentation among evaluated methods.
papers.selection_reason: Integrates 3D Gaussian Splatting with hierarchical 3D scene graphs for language-guided navigation, directly supporting embodied AI navigation and 3D scene understanding.
papers.title: PanoGraphGS: Unifying Panoptic Segmentation and Hierarchical 3D Scene Graphs with Gaussian Splatting
papers.tldr: PanoGraphGS jointly learns panoptic 3D Gaussian representations and hierarchical scene graphs for consistent, language-guided 3D scene understanding.

papers.abstract: Current state-of-the-art segmentation models still produce anatomically implausible shapes, such as broken vessels and fragmented glands, on the structures that are hardest to segment. Learned shape representations capture what structures look like and can help correct these errors, but most cover a fixed set of anatomical classes. Extending this coverage across classes and imaging modalities is costly because it often requires new voxel-level annotations. We propose Diffusion for Anatomical Reshaping with Text (DART), which learns a shared shape representation from segmentation probabilities. It uses anatomical descriptions to correct these probabilities without receiving medical images. Across 13 public benchmarks, absolute Dice gains reach 31% for individual gallbladder cases in CT and 10% for individual prostate cases in MRI. Using existing segmentation predictions, we scale a single shape representation from 50 to 377 anatomical classes without new voxel-level annotations for correction training. The shared representation also corrects four lesion classes absent from training and transfers from CT to MRI without retraining. Corrected labels also improve segmentation models, raising one model's Dice from 57.1% to 67.5%. The same pipeline supports annotations for 45,000 CT scans. These results suggest that sharing shape information within and across classes can reduce the need for new voxel-level annotations when extending segmentation to more anatomical classes and imaging modalities. The model is available at https://huggingface.co/Koushik45/DART-Seg
authors: Koushik Swarna, Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Lam Ngo, Wenxuan Li, Jiancheng Yang, Alan Yuille, Zongwei Zhou
bullets: Addresses broken or fragmented anatomical segmentations, especially for difficult structures.
Learns a shared shape representation from segmentation probabilities and anatomical descriptions, without using medical images during correction.
Scales from 50 to 377 anatomical classes using existing predictions, and transfers across CT and MRI without retraining.
Across 13 public benchmarks, reported Dice gains reach 31% for individual gallbladder CT cases and 10% for individual prostate MRI cases.
Corrected labels improve downstream segmentation, including one model’s Dice increase from 57.1% to 67.5%, and support annotation of 45,000 CT scans.
papers.selection_reason: Text-conditioned diffusion shape prior scales across anatomical classes and modalities; relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial/geometric priors.
papers.title: DART: Scaling a Shape Representation Across Anatomical Classes and Imaging Modalities
papers.tldr: DART uses text-guided diffusion to share anatomical shape knowledge across classes and imaging modalities, correcting implausible segmentation predictions without new voxel-level training annotations.

papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting grows a dense scene from a sparse initialization through adaptive density control (ADC), driven by per-Gaussian statistics gathered during rendering. These statistics pass a frustum-based visibility filter blind to occlusion: fully occluded Gaussians still count as observed, diluting the averaged gradient signal and suppressing densification precisely where geometry is occluded. We correct this with an occlusion-aware filter that restricts densification statistics to views in which a Gaussian actually contributes, and replace the criterion's raw view-count normalizer with an average-contribution one. Integrated into a StopThePop-based framework, the two together improve every image-quality metric over the occlusion-blind baseline on occlusion-heavy scenes (up to 6% lower LPIPS), at less than half the Gaussians a view-count normalizer requires. Under the longer schedules these large scenes require, the count stays bounded where most criteria diverge, and on smaller benchmarks our method stays competitive at a fraction of the competitors' count.
authors: Marcel Rogge, Ren\'e Schuster, Didier Stricker
bullets: Frustum visibility can count fully occluded Gaussians, weakening gradient statistics and suppressing needed densification.
The method filters statistics to views where a Gaussian actually contributes and normalizes by average contribution rather than raw view count.
Integrated with StopThePop, it improves all reported image-quality metrics on occlusion-heavy scenes, with up to 6% lower LPIPS.
It uses less than half as many Gaussians as a view-count normalizer and keeps counts bounded during longer training schedules.
On smaller benchmarks, it remains competitive while using a fraction of competitors’ Gaussian counts.
papers.selection_reason: Occlusion-aware densification for 3D Gaussian Splatting improves 3D scene representation, a key component of 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Counting Contributions, Not Views: Occlusion-Aware Densification for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.tldr: An occlusion-aware densification strategy for 3D Gaussian Splatting improves image quality while using substantially fewer Gaussians in heavily occluded scenes.

papers.abstract: Digital terrain maps (DTMs) are used for landing site selection, terrain-relative navigation, and geological analysis in planetary exploration. Existing state-of-practice reconstruction techniques for creating DTMs from satellite imagery use multi-view stereo, requiring complex pipelines for dealing with camera error, changing illumination, and images with limited disparity. This work introduces Orbital Terrain Networks (OrTeN), a DTM construction method that uses neural inverse rendering to jointly optimize a textured height map and orbital camera corrections from line-scan satellite images. OrTeN operates directly on calibrated line-scan images with pixel values expressed as radiance factor (I/F) and corrects both broad trajectory pose inconsistencies and high-frequency pointing jitter jointly with surface reconstruction during training. Surface-projected patch normalized cross-correlation (NCC) enforces consistency between observations of the same terrain, refining an initial rough reconstruction. A semi-empirical reflectance model and shadow rendering are used to fit surface appearance from multi-date imagery with differing solar illumination. OrTeN requires only calibrated line-scan images and initial camera poses and does not use any structural priors including ranging/depth measurements or initial rough DTMs. OrTeN is evaluated on four planetary imagery datasets. Aligned terrain RMSEs are 2.35 m at Jezero Crater, 2.82 m at Gale Crater, 16.18 m at Olympus Mons, and 0.43 m at McGetchin Crater.
bullets: Targets DTM generation from satellite imagery affected by camera errors, changing illumination, and limited image disparity.
Optimizes a textured height map together with broad trajectory corrections and high-frequency pointing jitter.
Uses surface-projected patch NCC, a reflectance model, and shadow rendering to enforce cross-image consistency across illumination conditions.
Requires calibrated line-scan images and initial camera poses, but no ranging/depth data or structural terrain priors.
Evaluated on four planetary datasets, with aligned terrain RMSEs ranging from 0.43 m to 16.18 m.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces OrTeN, a neural inverse graphics method for joint terrain and camera trajectory reconstruction, which is directly applicable to robot navigation in planetary exploration.
papers.title: OrTeN: Neural Inverse Graphics for Joint Terrain and Line-scan Camera Trajectory Reconstruction
papers.tldr: OrTeN jointly reconstructs planetary terrain and corrects line-scan satellite camera trajectories using neural inverse rendering, without depth measurements or an initial terrain model.

papers.abstract: Sparse-view novel view synthesis (NVS) is essential for AR/VR and real-time communication applications, yet remains challenging when reconstructing 3D scenes from limited viewpoints. While 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) excels in dense-view scenarios, it suffers from overfitting and geometry degradation under sparse inputs. Current approaches often tackle these problems from a local perspective, addressing either data quality or training regularization individually, lacking a unified and interpretable framework for systematic improvement. We introduce a new perspective that reframes sparse-view 3DGS from a few-shot learning viewpoint, treating each Gaussian primitive as a neuron and leveraging deep learning regularization techniques. Under this unified framework, our approach generates more effective supervision from scarce observations through two strategies: (1) data-related supervision enrichment via optical flow-guided pseudo-view synthesis and joint camera-scene optimization; and (2) training-time regularization via motion-aware dropout and early stopping, which suppress overfitting while preserving dynamic-scene stability. Extensive experiments on the SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 volumetric video challenge sparse-view dataset demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art optimization-based and feed-forward baselines. Our system won first place in the sparse-view track of the SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 challenge.
authors: Lejia Ye, Bin Wu, Jingjing Gao, Yiyang Wu, Xiaohu Zhang
bullets: Reframes each 3D Gaussian primitive as a neuron, providing a unified perspective on sparse-view reconstruction.
Enriches supervision with optical flow-guided pseudo-view synthesis and joint camera-scene optimization.
Uses motion-aware dropout and early stopping to suppress overfitting while maintaining dynamic-scene stability.
Outperforms reported optimization-based and feed-forward baselines on the SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 volumetric video challenge sparse-view dataset.
Won first place in the challenge’s sparse-view track.
papers.selection_reason: Improves 3D Gaussian Splatting for sparse-view novel view synthesis using a few-shot learning perspective and regularization techniques. This advances 3D foundation models for reconstruction.
papers.title: Rethinking Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting: A Few-Shot Learning Perspective on Overfitting Prevention
papers.tldr: A few-shot learning framework improves sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by enriching supervision and regularizing training to reduce overfitting and geometry degradation.

papers.abstract: Camera-based 3D semantic occupancy models can be trained without 3D labels by rendering their predictions into the images and supervising them with 2D pseudo labels. In sparse Gaussian representations trained this way, Gaussian positions are learned only through pixel-wise rendering losses, which we hypothesize give small foreground objects little weight. In trained GaussianFlowOcc models, the Gaussian density on foreground voxels is on average only 1.62 times that on background voxels. We propose a training-only foreground attraction loss that back-projects foreground pseudo-label pixels with pseudo depth and pulls nearby Gaussians toward these 3D points, favoring Gaussians that already predict the target class; the inference network is unchanged. On Occ3D-nuScenes, the loss raises this concentration to 2.40 over three seeds. Over three seeds, the mean foreground IoU increases from 6.29 to 6.96 and is higher for each seed, whereas the change in mean mIoU (13.53 to 13.82) is within the seed-to-seed variation of the baseline. Single-run ablations further indicate that pseudo-label targets outperform targets placed at ground-truth voxels and that acting on the Gaussian positions alone is not sufficient, and a single-seed test shows that the model degrades less when fewer Gaussians are kept at inference.
bullets: Weak 2D rendering supervision underweights foreground objects, leaving foreground Gaussian density only 1.62× that of background voxels.
The proposed loss back-projects foreground pseudo-label pixels using pseudo-depth and pulls nearby, class-compatible Gaussians toward them during training.
On Occ3D-nuScenes, foreground density rises to 2.40× background density, and mean foreground IoU improves from 6.29 to 6.96 across three seeds.
Mean mIoU increases only from 13.53 to 13.82, within baseline seed-to-seed variation.
Ablations favor pseudo-label targets over ground-truth voxel targets; the method also shows less degradation when fewer Gaussians are retained at inference.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a foreground attraction loss to improve the training of camera-based 3D occupancy models using sparse Gaussian representations, a technique relevant to 3D scene understanding.
papers.title: Where Do the Gaussians Go? Foreground Attraction for Camera-Based Weakly Supervised 3D Occupancy
papers.tldr: A training-only foreground attraction loss improves small-object occupancy localization and foreground IoU in weakly supervised Gaussian-based 3D occupancy models, with limited overall mIoU gains.

papers.abstract: We introduce ReDT, a feed-forward visual geometry transformer designed to scale multi-view reconstruction to high-definition (HD) inputs. Existing visual geometry transformers are typically trained at fixed, standard definition (SD) resolutions and exhibit degraded reconstruction quality and poor computational scaling to high input resolutions. While recent efficient architectures reduce the complexity of inter-frame attention, expensive intra-frame and encoder attention remain largely unaddressed, making HD reconstruction impractical with existing architectures. ReDT addresses both limitations with a resolution-aware architecture designed to scale to high-resolution inputs. The key idea of ReDT is to first map each view to a fixed-size set of basis tokens, compute correspondences in this compact constant-size basis space, and then project the outputs back to the original resolution for dense prediction. By decoupling the internal representation from input resolution during attention, ReDT substantially reduces the computational cost of high-resolution 3D reconstruction and improves model performance at all resolutions. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets spanning SD to FHD (2K) show that ReDT outperforms state-of-the-art visual geometry transformers in both reconstruction quality and computational efficiency. For instance, on the ETH3D (2K) dataset, ReDT achieves a $16\times$ speedup, a $34\%$ reduction in peak GPU memory usage, and a $33\%$ reduction in chamfer distance over VGGT-$\Omega$. \href{https://redt.github.io}{Project Website.}
authors: Abteen Arab, Guile Wu, Dongfeng Bai
bullets: Existing visual geometry transformers scale poorly to HD inputs because intra-frame and encoder attention remain expensive.
ReDT maps each view to a fixed-size set of basis tokens, computes correspondences in this compact space, and projects results back for dense prediction.
Experiments across SD to FHD (2K) datasets show improved reconstruction quality and computational efficiency at all tested resolutions.
On ETH3D at 2K, ReDT reports 16× faster inference, 34% lower peak GPU memory, and 33% lower Chamfer distance than VGGT-Ω.
papers.selection_reason: Resolution-decoupled visual geometry transformer for efficient HD multi-view reconstruction; fits 3D foundation models and efficient attention.
papers.title: ReDT: Resolution-Decoupled Visual Geometry Transformer
papers.tldr: ReDT enables efficient high-resolution multi-view 3D reconstruction by decoupling attention computation from input resolution.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) promises instant scene reconstruction with high-quality novel-view synthesis. Yet, fine-grained geometry and appearance remain difficult to recover, motivating us to revisit how feed-forward models represent, aggregate, and refine detailed visual information. We introduce FineSplat, a feed-forward 3DGS framework built around fine-grained image patches. Since global multi-view attention becomes prohibitively expensive at such high token resolutions, we develop a dual-grouping strategy that combines two complementary forms of locality: view-wise grouping enables efficient interaction among neighboring views, while 3D spatial grouping reconnects geometrically related tokens that may never have interacted under view-wise grouping by lifting them into the 3D scene space. We further leverage reconstruction error as direct feedback, providing an explicit rendering-based signal to recover fine-grained structures and appearance, thereby overcoming the limitations of one-pass feed-forward prediction. Finally, a compact Gaussian generation scheme preserves the benefits of fine-grained features without unnecessarily increasing the number of primitives. Together, these designs enable FineSplat to recover richer geometry and appearance while remaining efficient and compact, achieving state-of-the-art results by a substantial margin, under the same or smaller Gaussian budgets than existing methods.
authors: Hyebin Kim, Hwasik Jeong, Joonhyuk Park, Gyeongjin Kang, Jungwoo Kim, Younghyun Kim, Eunbyung Park
bullets: Targets the difficulty of recovering fine-grained geometry and appearance in feed-forward 3DGS.
Uses view-wise grouping for efficient neighboring-view interaction and 3D spatial grouping to reconnect geometrically related tokens.
Uses rendering reconstruction error as explicit feedback to refine structures and appearance beyond one-pass prediction.
Generates a compact set of Gaussians to retain fine-detail benefits without unnecessarily increasing primitive counts.
Reports state-of-the-art performance by a substantial margin under the same or smaller Gaussian budgets, according to the abstract.
papers.selection_reason: Feed-forward 3DGS with dual-grouping attention and compact Gaussian generation; relevant to 3D reconstruction and efficient attention.
papers.title: FineSplat: Fine Patches, Local Groups, Detailed Splats
papers.tldr: FineSplat improves feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting by combining fine image patches, local view/3D grouping, reconstruction-error feedback, and compact Gaussian generation.

papers.abstract: We present Stable Signer V3, an interactive high-resolution sign language avatar system built on 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting. It addresses three limitations of existing avatars: restricted facial expression, inaccurate identity-specific body deformation, and loss of fine appearance details. Shared Face Primitive Splatting adds transferable superquadric primitives for richer expression control; Test-Time Body Primitive Splatting learns an identity-specific virtual muscle layer for more faithful motion; and Test-Time Tunneling Super-Resolution uses TunnelingNet to recover identity-specific high-resolution details. Both test-time modules are optimized once per signer identity; inference then runs entirely from the stored identity parameters. Together, they reduce facial geometry error by 71.4%, body-boundary error by 35.1% across ten identities, and high-resolution RGB reconstruction error by 24.2% on held-out evaluations, while retaining interactive streaming.
authors: Sen Fang, Liwei Che, Dimitris N. Metaxas
bullets: Addresses limited facial expression, inaccurate identity-specific deformation, and loss of fine visual detail in existing avatars.
Uses Shared Face Primitive Splatting for transferable expression control.
Applies Test-Time Body Primitive Splatting to learn a signer-specific virtual muscle layer, plus TunnelingNet-based super-resolution for identity-specific details.
Test-time modules are optimized once per signer; inference thereafter uses stored identity parameters while preserving interactive streaming.
Reports reductions of 71.4% in facial geometry error, 35.1% in body-boundary error across ten identities, and 24.2% in high-resolution RGB reconstruction error.
papers.selection_reason: Presents Stable Signer V3, a system for sign language production using 4D deformable primitive splatting. This directly connects visual and language understanding to physical actions (avatar generation), fitting Vision-Language-Action and 3D Vision.
papers.title: Stable Signer V3: 4D Deformable Primitive Splatting Is All You Need for Sign Language Production
papers.tldr: Stable Signer V3 enables interactive, high-resolution sign-language avatars with richer expressions, more accurate signer-specific motion, and finer appearance details using 4D deformable primitive splatting.

papers.abstract: Recovering metric 3D geometry from images is fundamentally ill-posed due to perspective projection ambiguity. Current geometry models incorporate supplied or predicted intrinsics during inference, but do not use them to supervise model adaptation. To refine these predictions, test-time adaptation (TTA) typically relies on external depth measurements. In this paper, we instead use camera intrinsics as an output-side geometric verifier. Comparing the point cloud's viewing rays with those defined by the known intrinsics yields a direct measure of geometric inconsistency. We propose \textit{IntriAdapt}, a TTA framework that minimizes this closed-form geometric residual. By optimizing a lightweight LoRA adapter on a frozen geometry foundation model, our method aligns the prediction with the specific camera model without depth sensors or external priors. We further extend this approach to video sequences, demonstrating that adapting a short sequence generalizes to other sequences captured by the same camera. The adapted model processes held-out images in a feed-forward pass, without repeating optimization for each frame. Experiments on ten single-image and seven sequence benchmarks across multiple base models show that \textit{IntriAdapt} consistently outperforms both unadapted and oracle-intrinsics baselines in metric accuracy and relative geometry.
authors: Jiaxing Chen, Zizheng Yan, Jingyu Zhuang, Jinwei Chen, Shuguang Cui, Guanying Chen, Qingnan Fan
bullets: Addresses perspective ambiguity in image-based metric 3D geometry estimation.
Minimizes a closed-form residual between predicted point-cloud viewing rays and rays implied by the camera intrinsics.
Optimizes a lightweight LoRA adapter while keeping the geometry foundation model frozen.
Sequence adaptation generalizes across images from the same camera, enabling feed-forward inference on held-out frames.
Across ten single-image and seven sequence benchmarks, it outperforms unadapted and oracle-intrinsics baselines in metric accuracy and relative geometry.
papers.selection_reason: Test-time adaptation for metric geometry estimation using camera intrinsics; fits TTA and 3D foundation models.
papers.title: IntriAdapt: Generalizable Intrinsic-Guided Test-Time Adaptation for Metric Geometry Estimation
papers.tldr: IntriAdapt improves metric 3D geometry at test time by using known camera intrinsics as a geometric consistency signal, without depth sensors or external priors.

papers.abstract: Recent 3D Large Language Models (3D-LLMs) have shown strong performance on scene question answering with extensive post-training. Yet, existing benchmarks rarely evaluate how 3D-LLMs respond to referential ambiguity, insufficient scene evidence, or false presuppositions, obscuring whether their responses are grounded in 3D evidence. In this work, we introduce UNICORNS, a benchmark for evaluating the reliability of 3D-LLM responses across four evidence conditions. UNICORNS contains 11,387 questions across 557 ScanNet scans, covering eight challenge categories alongside answerable controls. A response passes only if it satisfies the required response behavior and contains no scene claim unsupported by the available evidence. Evaluation of six open-sourced 3D-LLMs reveals a pronounced performance gap: even the strongest zero-shot model achieves 61.22% accuracy on answerable controls, but only 40.94% across the eight challenge categories. To address this gap, we further propose HORN, an obligation-aware post-training method combining group-relative task rewards, leaf-conditioned obligation rewards, and supervised control replay. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HORN reaches $75.1 \pm 1.0\%$ across the challenge categories and $77.2 \pm 0.8\%$ overall, outperforming all baselines without degrading answerable-control accuracy. Our findings enable a systematic evaluation and improvement of evidence-grounded 3D reasoning for 3D-LLMs (code: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/unicorns-6B38/).
authors: Yifei Zhao, Fanyu Zhao, Han Zhang, Yixuan Lin, Yuyang Hou, Bin Wu, Ruike Cao, Li Xiao, Yinsheng Li
bullets: Introduces UNICORNS, a benchmark with 11,387 questions across 557 ScanNet scans and four evidence conditions.
Tests referential ambiguity, insufficient evidence, false presuppositions, and related challenges using eight categories plus answerable controls.
Six open-source 3D-LLMs show a large reliability gap: 61.22% on controls versus 40.94% on challenge categories for the strongest zero-shot model.
Proposes HORN, an obligation-aware post-training method using task, obligation, and supervised control-replay rewards.
HORN achieves 75.1 ± 1.0% on challenges and 77.2 ± 0.8% overall, without degrading control accuracy.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark and post-training for evidence-grounded 3D-LLM reasoning; directly targets 3D foundation models and spatial multimodal reasoning.
papers.title: Do 3D Large Language Models Really Use 3D Evidence?
papers.tldr: UNICORNS reveals that 3D-LLMs often fail to ground answers in available 3D evidence, while HORN substantially improves reliable reasoning without hurting answerable-question performance.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have enabled them to act as autonomous agents, creating and editing 3D models via code or direct software manipulation. In practical workflows, these models must infer object shapes, materials, spatial layouts, and lighting from diverse references while strictly following instructions to reconstruct, modify, or design 3D content. However, existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of such open-ended requests across real-world scenarios. To bridge this gap, we introduce BlenderWorld, the first comprehensive benchmark dedicated to evaluating frontier models on realistic 3D creation tasks. BlenderWorld comprises 223 tasks spanning architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization, driven by text, image, video, and structured specification inputs. To rigorously assess these complex deliverables, we establish a unified evaluation protocol: we render the submitted Blender projects from multiple viewpoints and evaluate them against 2,651 task-specific binary rubrics alongside holistic visual quality scores. Benchmarking thirteen frontier models reveals that GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest overall fused score of 79.9, followed by Opus-5 (73.0) and GPT-5.6-Sol (67.7). Ultimately, our findings reveal a critical bottleneck: while current models can parse broad instructions, they still profoundly struggle with fine-grained 3D spatial coherence and accurate structural reproduction in Blender, leaving substantial headroom for future 3D-native agentics.
authors: Xinyu Fang, Yuchi Wang, Weihao Yu, Rongyao Fang, Zhaohai Li, Zhixun Li, Tiancheng Gu, Xilin Wei, Yuhang Zang, Hongsheng Li, Dahua Lin, Guofeng Zhang, Shuai Bai, Zhibo Yang, Dayiheng Liu
bullets: Introduces 223 open-ended tasks across architecture, products, natural environments, and scientific visualization.
Uses text, image, video, and structured specifications as task inputs.
Evaluates rendered Blender projects from multiple viewpoints with 2,651 binary rubrics and holistic visual-quality scores.
Among 13 frontier models, GPT-6-Astra achieves the highest reported fused score, followed by Opus-5 and GPT-5.6-Sol.
Results show broad instruction understanding but substantial weaknesses in structural accuracy and 3D spatial consistency.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for MLLM agents on 3D creation, emphasizing spatial coherence; fits spatial intelligence and 3D foundation model evaluation.
papers.title: BlenderWorld: Benchmarking Visual Agents for 3D Creation from Real-World References
papers.tldr: BlenderWorld benchmarks multimodal agents on realistic Blender-based 3D creation and finds that models still struggle with fine-grained spatial coherence and faithful reconstruction.

papers.abstract: We present RhinoNet, a simplicial complex-based point cloud neural network, that creates a geometry-preserving embedding of high-dimensional point clouds. RhinoNet takes collections of datasets, also called {\em data cohorts}, and processes each dataset (point cloud) within the cohort as a simplicial complex. These simplicial complexes have datapoints as vertices and edges learned by Vietoris-Rips filtration. Using simplicial wavelets and MLP layers, RhinoNet computes a vector representation of each dataset in a latent space produced by an autoencoder. The latent space is optimized such that an optimal transport distance between pairs of point clouds is preserved between the latent representations. We apply RhinoNet to single-cell datasets collected on patients---a common source of such high-dimensional data. RhinoNet creates a patient level representation, known in biological contexts as a phenoscape. We establish that RhinoNet generates organized phenoscapes, whereas other methods such as static maps do not. Next we show that we can generate entire point clouds by sampling and decoding this phenoscape. We show two modes of generation via 1) latent flow matching and 2) geodesic interpolation in latent space, followed by a decoding back into the point cloud space. RhinoNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on single-cell and spatial data cohorts relative to tested baselines. Overall, RhinoNet lifts the concepts of representation learning and generative modeling to the point cloud or population level and defines a neural model for phenoscaping.
authors: Siddharth Viswanath, Hiren Madhu, Eddie Cavallin, Benjamin Jones, Alistair Wilkinson, Christopher Tape, Michael Perlmutter, Rex Ying, Ian Adelstein, Smita Krishnaswamy
bullets: Processes each dataset as a Vietoris–Rips simplicial complex with datapoints as vertices and learned edges.
Uses simplicial wavelets, MLP layers, and an autoencoder to encode datasets into a latent phenoscape.
Optimizes latent representations to preserve optimal-transport distances between point clouds.
Generates point clouds through latent flow matching or geodesic interpolation followed by decoding.
Applied to single-cell and spatial data cohorts, achieving state-of-the-art performance against tested baselines and producing organized phenoscap es.
papers.selection_reason: Connects geometric topological analysis to latent point-cloud models and environment generation; relevant to 3D representation and world-model-style latent dynamics.
papers.title: RhinoNet: Unsupervised Learning for Phenoscaping and Generation of High Dimensional Point Clouds
papers.tldr: RhinoNet learns geometry-preserving, patient-level representations of high-dimensional point-cloud datasets and can generate new point clouds from the learned latent space.

papers.abstract: Geometric and Semantic Foundation models are becoming increasingly popular tools for generating spatial maps for robots. Recent work (e.g., FOUND-IT) has leveraged these tools to construct real-time, task-driven, and open-set 3D scene graphs from a single uncalibrated camera. However, while classical robot mapping techniques have undergone extensive system demonstrations, limited work has been done to develop both the fundamental and the systems wide advancements needed to integrate these new types of robot spatial memory into a full, useable autonomy pipeline. In this paper, we bridge this gap, and in doing so we also evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of this type of 3D memory. Towards this end, we integrate FOUND-IT into a mobile manipulator platform and demonstrate it is well-suited to support multiple objectives such as object change detection, support for multiple mapping sessions, determination of navigable paths, and directly support object grasping for the task of scene re-arrangement. Furthermore, we provide nuanced insights into the effectiveness and limitations of a monocular, foundation-model-driven 3D scene graph construction system using observations from rigorous on-robot experiments. Code is available at https://github. com/MIT-SPARK/FOUND-IT.
authors: Dominic Maggio, Lorenzo Shaikewitz, Aryan Naveen, Kris Hauser, Luca Carlone
bullets: Addresses the gap between foundation-model-based 3D mapping and complete robot autonomy pipelines.
Integrates FOUND-IT with a mobile manipulator using a single uncalibrated camera.
Supports object change detection, multiple mapping sessions, navigable-path reasoning, and grasping for scene rearrangement.
Reports rigorous on-robot experiments assessing the system’s effectiveness and limitations.
The scope is constrained by the limitations of monocular, foundation-model-driven 3D scene graph construction.
papers.selection_reason: The paper presents a system (FOUND-IT) that leverages geometric and semantic foundation models to construct 3D scene graphs for a mobile manipulator. It demonstrates the integration of this memory system into a full autonomy pipeline for tasks like object grasping, path planning, and scene rearrangement, directly fitting 3D foundation models, robot manipulation, and embodied memory.
papers.title: Foundation-Model-Driven 3D Scene Graphs for Mobile Manipulation
papers.tldr: The paper integrates a monocular, foundation-model-driven 3D scene graph system into a mobile manipulator and evaluates its usefulness for end-to-end spatially informed tasks.

papers.abstract: Cage-based deformation (CBD) parametrises 3D geometry through a small set of control handles, effectively enabling a variety of tasks from animation and interactive modelling to tool-based co-design, neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic shape optimization. Many optimization approaches relying on CBD employ regularisation strategies to reduce the distortion of the deformed mesh by encouraging smooth, regular cage deformations. These techniques offer soft guidance to an optimization algorithm towards desirable deformations, but compete with the task objective rather than changing the deformation parameterization itself. In this work we introduce Structural Affinity for CBD, an explicit regularisation method which enables smooth deformations through control cages by exploiting a two-cage structure to couple cage-handle motion directly. Structural Affinity precomputes an affinity matrix using mean-value coordinates, binding the inner control-cage to a coarser outer-cage. This matrix defines how much a cage handle displacement propagates to neighbouring handles which substantially decreases and often eliminates cage self-intersections, reduces mesh distortion, and adds linear overhead at deformation time. Across robotic control--morphology co-design, source-to-target neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic wing shape optimization, Structural Affinity produces more regular deformations and substantially reduces reliance on hand-designed structural loss terms. We report consistent gains on three complementary diagnostics: the cotangent Laplacian, a proxy for surface smoothness; cage distortion, capturing whether control handles move coherently; and surface roughness, which measures undesirable oscillation in wing geometry.
authors: Aviraj Newatia, Shengan Yang, Hantao Zhong, Rika Antonova
bullets: Addresses self-intersections, irregular cage motion, and mesh distortion in cage-based deformation optimization.
Uses a precomputed mean-value-coordinate affinity matrix to propagate handle displacements between two nested cages.
Adds only linear overhead during deformation and reduces reliance on hand-designed structural losses.
Demonstrates consistent improvements in cotangent-Laplacian smoothness, cage distortion, and surface roughness across robotics, neural deformation transfer, and aerodynamic wing optimization.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces Structural Affinity for cage-based 3D shape design, relevant to 3D vision and robotics control-morphology co-design.
papers.title: Structural Affinity: An Algorithm for Coherent Cage-Based Shape Design
papers.tldr: Structural Affinity improves cage-based 3D deformation by coupling a fine inner cage to a coarser outer cage, producing smoother, more coherent shapes with less distortion.

papers.abstract: Recent progress in 3D generation has motivated growing interest in compact generative representations of complex 3D scenes. For native 3D Gaussian scenes, however, learning such representations remains challenging due to widely varying primitive counts, nonuniform spatial density, and differences in geometry and appearance even among spatially neighboring primitives. In this work, we introduce TriFold, a native 3D Gaussian VAE that encodes Gaussian scenes into a fixed-layout triplane latent and jointly reconstructs their geometry and appearance. The key insight is to impose structural regularity on the latent space while preserving the spatial adaptivity of the underlying Gaussians. During encoding, we use cell-wise learned queries to aggregate projected Gaussians into multiple slots per cell, reducing the information loss caused by single-feature pooling. During decoding, occupancy prediction identifies active regions, where query-based set prediction and candidate selection reconstruct local Gaussian sets with spatially varying primitive counts.
