Building on this representation, we train a latent flow-matching model for conditional scene-level 3DGS generation, enabling point-cloud-conditioned synthesis and single-image-conditioned amodal generation. Experiments demonstrate that TriFold achieves high-fidelity reconstruction and generation from a single image that provides only a partial observation of the scene, validating its effectiveness for native 3D Gaussian representation learning. https://fantasy-amap.github.io/TriFold
authors: Yun Wang, Chiyu Wang, Fan Jiang, Ziyu Zhu, Zhaoxu Sun, Guangchi Fang, Mu Xu, Dapeng Wu
bullets: Addresses variable primitive counts, uneven spatial density, and heterogeneous geometry and appearance in native 3D Gaussian scenes.
Uses cell-wise learned queries with multiple slots to aggregate projected Gaussians while reducing information loss.
Decodes with occupancy prediction, query-based set prediction, and candidate selection to reconstruct spatially varying local Gaussian sets.
Trains a latent flow-matching model for point-cloud-conditioned synthesis and single-image-conditioned amodal generation.
Experiments show high-fidelity reconstruction and single-image-conditioned generation from partial scene observations.
papers.selection_reason: Native 3D Gaussian VAE with structured latent and generative scene modeling; relevant to 3D foundation models and generation.
papers.title: TriFold: Folding irregular 3D Gaussians into structured latents for 3D Scene Generation
papers.tldr: TriFold converts irregular 3D Gaussian scenes into structured triplane latents for high-fidelity reconstruction and conditional scene generation.

papers.abstract: N-dimensional splatting extends 3D Gaussian Splatting with view direction and time to model view-dependent and dynamic effects. Each primitive is lifted into a joint distribution over position and conditioning variables, then conditionally sliced at each rendering query. N-DGS and UBS share this step across Gaussian and Beta kernels: recovering the conditional mean, opacity, and covariance requires per-primitive matrix inversions and regression products in every forward pass. We introduce direct conditional parameterization, replacing this covariance-derived readout with explicit per-effect parameters: a Cholesky precision factor for opacity and a factorized query-to-position regression operator with learnable per-dimension coupling. Unrestricted conditional coordinates recover a valid joint covariance; our factorization adds spatial-scale and coupling priors. Applied to both kernels, the parameterization yields dGS (Gaussian) and dBS (Beta). Across five static and dynamic benchmarks, they match or exceed their covariance-derived counterparts on quality, with gains up to +1.26 dB in the main MCMC evaluation. Production slicing is 6.9-7.7 times faster than on-the-fly covariance-derived conditioning; complete-render profiling gives 1.25-1.91 times speedups on four trained scenes. Direct conditioning provides a structured, kernel-agnostic alternative for N-dimensional splatting. Project page: https://gaozhongpai.github.io/dgs/.
authors: Zhongpai Gao, Benjamin Planche, Van Nguyen Nguyen, Meng Zheng, Anwesa Choudhuri, Arun Innanje, Terrence Chen, Ziyan Wu
bullets: N-dimensional splatting models view-dependent and dynamic effects by conditioning primitives on query variables.
The method replaces per-query covariance inversions and regression products with explicit Cholesky precision and factorized query-to-position parameters.
Applied to Gaussian and Beta kernels, it produces dGS and dBS with structured spatial-scale and coupling priors.
Across five static and dynamic benchmarks, quality matches or exceeds covariance-derived methods, with gains up to 1.26 dB.
Production slicing is 6.9–7.7× faster, while complete rendering is 1.25–1.91× faster on four trained scenes.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces direct conditional parameterization for N-dimensional splatting, a significant technical contribution to 3D Foundation Models.
papers.title: Direct Conditional Parameterization for N-Dimensional Splatting
papers.tldr: Direct conditional parameterization makes N-dimensional Gaussian and Beta splatting substantially faster while matching or improving rendering quality.

papers.abstract: Internet-scale photo collections of real-world landmarks have driven progress in 3D computer vision yet remain highly challenging for modern 3D foundation models (3DFMs) that estimate scene structure in a single feed-forward pass. In this work, we introduce ArchWorld, a benchmark of 3D architectural landmarks with high geographic coverage and rich metadata. We use this benchmark to conduct a thorough error analysis of current 3DFMs to understand where they fall short and how they can be improved. We examine socially relevant disparities in model error and find that model performance varies by geographic region; however, unlike typical fairness regimes, the trends only partially match training data representation. Our investigation reveals that the observed geographic disparities reflect not only differences in data representation and scene size but also differences in region-specific architectural features and background distractors that make scenes from different regions inherently vary in difficulty. Leveraging insights from these model failings, we introduce an intervention scheme that improves 3DFM performance while simultaneously reducing geographic disparities.
authors: Nicky Kriplani, Yiwen Zhang, Angelina Wang, Hadar Averbuch-Elor
bullets: Introduces ArchWorld, a landmark benchmark with broad geographic coverage and rich metadata.
Analyzes errors in single-pass 3D foundation models and identifies region-dependent performance differences.
Finds that disparities reflect data representation, scene size, architectural features, and background distractors.
Shows that geographic error trends only partially align with training-data representation.
Develops an intervention scheme that improves model performance and reduces geographic disparities.
papers.selection_reason: Directly studies 3D foundation models, analyzing geographic disparities and proposing an intervention to improve reconstruction performance.
papers.title: Towards Reconstructing Geographically Diverse Architecture with 3D Foundation Models
papers.tldr: ArchWorld benchmarks geographically diverse architectural landmarks, diagnoses regional disparities in 3D foundation models, and presents an intervention that improves performance while reducing those disparities.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward transformer models have recently achieved strong performance in multi-view 3D reconstruction, but they still rely primarily on appearance-based attention and often struggle in dynamic scenes with weak geometric cues. In this work, we introduce a motion- and gravity-aware framework under the Learning Using Privileged Information (LUPI) paradigm. During training, residual optical flow and gravity direction are provided as privileged signals to guide geometric representation learning; during inference, the model uses standard visual inputs only. We integrate these priors into transformer backbones with lightweight architectural changes, preserving feed-forward efficiency. Experiments on standard benchmarks show consistent gains in reconstruction accuracy and robustness, especially in scenes with dynamic objects, ambiguous structure, and challenging camera motion. Our analysis further shows that the optimal injection stage is backbone-dependent: middle-layer integration is generally preferable for VGGT, while late-stage integration is more effective for {\pi}3. These results suggest that LUPI offers a practical way to inject motion and physical priors into feed-forward 3D reconstruction without increasing test-time complexity.
authors: Shiyao Qian, Yuan Ren, Dongfeng Bai
bullets: Targets weak geometric cues and dynamic-scene challenges in appearance-driven multi-view reconstruction.
Uses residual optical flow and gravity direction as privileged training signals, while inference relies only on standard visual inputs.
Adds these priors to transformer backbones through lightweight architectural changes.
Standard-benchmark experiments report consistent gains, particularly with dynamic objects, ambiguous structure, and difficult camera motion.
Prior injection works best at different stages depending on the backbone: middle layers for VGGT and late layers for π3.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a motion- and gravity-aware framework for feed-forward 3D reconstruction using transformer backbones and privileged information, relevant to 3D vision and foundation models.
papers.title: Motion- and Gravity-Aware Feedforward 3D Reconstruction
papers.tldr: A LUPI-based feed-forward 3D reconstruction framework uses training-only motion and gravity cues to improve accuracy and robustness without adding inference-time inputs or complexity.

papers.abstract: Language-guided 3D affordance grounding aims to localize functional regions on 3D objects according to interaction intents. However, existing methods exhibit poor generalization to unseen objects. One challenge is the query-target gap: a semantic discrepancy between query features encoding interaction intents and target-region features, leading to inaccurate grounding. End-to-end training favors query representations tailored to seen objects, limiting their compatibility with shifted target-region features on unseen objects. To address this issue, we propose BridgeAfford, a framework that reduces the query-target semantic gap from two complementary perspectives. First, Interaction Region Alignment (IRA) promotes cross-object alignment among geometrically similar interaction regions during training. This enables structures on unseen objects that resemble previously observed ones to produce representations similar to those learned during training, facilitating target-region recognition. Second, Visual Evidence Aggregation (VEA) leverages a 2D affordance model to refine the attention distribution and guide the query toward the correct region, yielding more target-aware queries. Extensive experiments on the LASO and PIAD datasets demonstrate that BridgeAfford outperforms existing methods, particularly on unseen objects, highlighting its robust generalization ability.
authors: Yijie Su, Yakun Zhu, Yi Bin, Pengpeng Zeng, Liang Chen, Guoqing Wang, Jingkuan Song, Heng Tao Shen
bullets: Targets poor generalization caused by mismatched query and target-region representations.
Interaction Region Alignment aligns geometrically similar interaction regions across objects during training.
Visual Evidence Aggregation uses a 2D affordance model to refine attention and make queries more target-aware.
Experiments on LASO and PIAD show improved performance, especially for unseen objects.
Scope: focuses on generalization to shifted or previously unseen 3D objects.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes BridgeAfford for generalizable 3D affordance grounding, addressing the query-target gap and generalization in 3D foundation models.
papers.title: BridgeAfford: Bridging Query-Target Gap for Generalizable 3D Affordance Grounding
papers.tldr: BridgeAfford improves language-guided 3D affordance grounding on unseen objects by narrowing the semantic gap between interaction queries and target regions.

papers.abstract: Generating 3D assets with explicit parts requires two properties at once: geometric detail inside each part and structural coherence across the whole object. Recent image-conditioned 3D generation models adopt a structured 3D representation that anchors tokens to explicit spatial positions, capturing both properties, but their output remains a single fused mesh. We ask how a part-decomposed generation model can inherit both properties of these holistic priors, and answer with STRUCTPARTS, a framework whose core technical contribution is a dual-frame coordinate interleaving mechanism: each shape latent is interpreted under both a part-local and an object-global reference frame, and processed through a global-local inter-leaved transformer that simultaneously reuses the prior's geometric detail at the part scale and its structural coherence at the whole-object scale. As its structural input, STRUCTPARTS uses a segmented mesh scaffold, a coarse mesh paired with a face-level segmentation mask kept entirely within the prior's native 3D representation. With only lightweight finetuning, both intra-part detail and inter-part coherence emerge from the same pretrained weights. On PartObjaverse-Tiny, STRUCTPARTS matches or surpasses prior part-decomposed models at a fraction of their training cost, while naturally supporting part-mesh refinement and part-level editing.
authors: Yiqun Zhao, Binbin Huang, Haobin Duan, Zibo Zhao, Shenghua Gao
bullets: Addresses the challenge of combining fine intra-part geometry with whole-object structural coherence.
Uses dual-frame coordinate interleaving, interpreting latents in both part-local and object-global frames.
A global-local interleaved transformer transfers geometric detail and structural coherence from pretrained holistic priors.
Conditions generation on a segmented mesh scaffold represented in the prior’s native 3D format.
On PartObjaverse-Tiny, matches or exceeds prior part-decomposed models with substantially lower training cost and supports part refinement and editing.
papers.selection_reason: Reuses holistic 3D priors for part-decomposed generation, fitting 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Seeing Both the Forest and the Trees: Reusing Holistic 3D Priors for Part-Decomposed Generation
papers.tldr: STRUCTPARTS reuses holistic 3D generation priors to produce detailed, structurally coherent, part-decomposed 3D assets with lightweight finetuning.

papers.abstract: Real-time mobile volumetric video enables immersive free-viewpoint experiences, but delivering high-quality 3D content under constrained bandwidth and computation remains challenging. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) systems, such as V$^3$, enable efficient mobile streaming by encoding time-varying Gaussian attributes with commodity video codecs and hardware decoding. However, existing pipelines treat all Gaussians as frame-varying signals, which is poorly suited to full-scene content where large portions remain temporally stable. Our empirical study shows that frame-wise adaptation and video coding of all Gaussians cause quality degradation in complex full-scene content, particularly in temporally stable regions. To address this issue, we propose ResStreamGS, a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that processes Gaussians according to their temporal behavior. ResStreamGS identifies residual-sensitive primitives through lightweight probe adaptation and reuses stable Gaussians within each Group of Pictures (GOP). Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP, while only residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in the frame-wise hardware-decodable video stream. Experiments on complex full-scene volumetric videos show that ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51--8.35~dB over a controlled V$^3$-style all-Gaussians baseline, reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5%, and achieves 30.883~FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.
authors: Haoran Liu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Hengyuan Na, Miao Hu, Guocong Quan
bullets: Targets quality degradation and bandwidth/computation inefficiency when all Gaussians are treated as frame-varying.
Uses lightweight probe adaptation to identify residual-sensitive Gaussian primitives.
Transmits stable Gaussians once per GOP and keeps only residual-sensitive Gaussians in the frame-wise hardware-decodable stream.
On complex full-scene videos, improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51–8.35 dB and reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5% versus a controlled V$^3$-style baseline.
Reaches 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes ResStreamGS for efficient mobile volumetric video streaming using 3D Gaussian Splatting, addressing both 3D foundation models and video generation efficiency.
papers.title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
papers.tldr: ResStreamGS improves mobile volumetric video streaming by separating temporally stable Gaussians from residual-sensitive ones, reducing payload while enhancing reconstructed quality and maintaining real-time performance.

papers.abstract: We identify a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks. We prove that standard masking triggers a topological collapse, effectively forcing the model to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. To resolve this, we introduce SIEVE (Scalar Invariant Extraction Via Equivariance), an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework that compresses point cloud geometry into invariant scalar embeddings. At its core is the spherical projection mask, which preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics, sidestepping the obstruction by construction. Experiments confirm that SIEVE circumvents the predicted collapse where constant and noise masks fail. On downstream point cloud tasks, the resulting embeddings improve over coordinate-based baselines and hand-crafted geometric descriptors, with the largest gains on generalization to unseen shape categories.
authors: Jongann Lee, Sun Woo Park, Yun Young Choi
bullets: Standard masking is theoretically incompatible with SE(3)-equivariant networks because it removes the reference needed to infer orientation.
SIEVE extracts geometry into SE(3)-invariant scalar embeddings.
Its spherical projection mask preserves global pose while hiding local semantics.
Experiments show SIEVE avoids the collapse observed with constant and noise masks.
The embeddings outperform coordinate-based and hand-crafted geometric baselines, especially on unseen shape categories.
papers.selection_reason: SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised point-cloud learning with invariant scalar embeddings; relevant to 3D pretraining and geometric representation learning.
papers.title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: SIEVE avoids a topological collapse in equivariant point-cloud masked autoencoding by using pose-preserving spherical projection masks and invariant scalar embeddings.

papers.abstract: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. Experiments demonstrate strong image quality and geometric consistency in novel-view generation, alongside competitive 3D language understanding. Further analysis shows that joint training improves cross-view correspondence in VAE representations and similarity in a 3D-aware feature space.
authors: Jahyeok Koo, Hyeonseo Yu, Seungho Jang, Jaewoo Jung, Jiwon Kang, Seokju Cho, Seungryong Kim
bullets: Targets the challenge of preserving both scene appearance and spatial structure from limited observations.
Introduces Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal Mixture-of-Transformers model.
Encodes camera geometry in VAE and ViT representations and integrates understanding features via masked joint self-attention.
Achieves strong image quality and geometric consistency while maintaining competitive 3D language understanding.
Joint training improves cross-view correspondence and 3D-aware feature similarity.
papers.selection_reason: Investigates using 3D language understanding (spatial questions) to supervise novel-view generation. This combines 3D reasoning with generative models, relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
papers.tldr: Ask4NV uses 3D language understanding and camera-aware multimodal modeling to improve the visual quality and geometric consistency of novel-view generation.

papers.abstract: Anatomical labels help 3D Gaussian splatting preserve vessels in cinematic renderings of CT, but the representation is still found by optimising each patient's scene, where densification decides where Gaussians go, while real-time displays cap their number. We address one part of this process: deciding where a fixed budget of B Gaussians should be placed. We propose a reusable, labelaware allocation front end that maps a patient's CT, labels and transfer function to a density over 2mm cells and draws exactly B positions from it without per-patient optimisation; the other Gaussian attributes are still fitted per patient. The front end is learned once from per-patient optimised scenes and implemented as a population-trained neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF). With identical attribute fitting on 20 held-out patients at 10K-100K Gaussians, both raise vessel-masked PSNR over uniform allocation by 4.5-7.1dB and over pruning a dense voxel-aligned model by 1.6-3.3dB. The neural prior does not differ significantly from per-patient optimised allocation at any budget, and VACF is within 0.6dB of it on vessels; on 19 external patients the neural prior again matches it on vessels and VACF is within 0.7dB. As an initialisation for position optimisation, VACF allocation beats per-patient densification on vessels at 10K Gaussians and, at 25K, reaches a higher vessel PSNR after 118s of optimisation than densification after 248s. Under altered rendering presets, VACF transfers to new colours and lighting but not to a label-free transfer function, whereas the neural prior shows the opposite pattern.
authors: Bowen Xiang, Dingjie Su, Jon S. Heiselman, Michael I. Miga
bullets: Addresses budget-constrained Gaussian placement for cinematic CT rendering, while per-patient fitting still determines other Gaussian attributes.
Maps CT, anatomical labels, and a transfer function to a cell-level density and samples exactly B Gaussian positions.
Introduces a learned neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF), trained from optimised scenes.
Across held-out and external patients, both methods outperform uniform and dense-model-pruning allocations; the neural prior matches per-patient optimisation, while VACF remains close.
VACF improves vessel quality and optimisation speed as an initialisation, but transfer depends on the rendering setup and availability of labels.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses budget constraints in 3D Gaussian Splatting for medical imaging by proposing a reusable, label-aware allocation front end and neural prior.
papers.title: Where Should the Gaussians Go? Reusable Label-Aware Allocation for Budget-Constrained Gaussian Splatting of Cinematic CT
papers.tldr: A reusable label-aware Gaussian allocation strategy places a fixed rendering budget where CT vessels matter, improving vessel quality and speeding position optimisation without per-patient allocation search.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/
authors: Yongzhen Hu, Hao Yu, Jiawei Wang, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu, Xingliang Liu, Ruizhen Hu, Xiaowei Zhou, Hujun Bao, Sida Peng
bullets: Targets high-quality novel-view rendering from input images, especially under large viewpoint changes.
Decouples geometry and Gaussian-attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch.
Uses ground-truth camera poses for Gaussian alignment during training and large-angle target-view supervision.
Achieves the best mean LPIPS and DISTS among evaluated methods across six datasets in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings.
In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS improve by 25.8% and 32.9% versus the strongest evaluated baselines; scope is feed-forward reconstruction under the tested settings.
papers.selection_reason: Improves Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by decoupling geometry and attributes, achieving state-of-the-art rendering quality.
papers.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
papers.tldr: InfiniSplat v2 improves feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for large viewpoint changes by separating geometry and attribute learning and using stronger view-aware supervision.

papers.abstract: Large view synthesis models (LVSMs) reconstruct scenes from sparse views and render novel views quickly, but they incur unnecessary storage and rendering costs due to token redundancy. We present GLoD-LVSM, a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation for LVSMs with continuous levels of detail. First, instead of learning a fixed set of scene anchor initializations, GLoD-LVSM learns a continuous field that initializes a flexible number of anchors to match the desired budget. A condenser then aggregates scene information into these anchors, with both the field and condenser trained end-to-end. Second, the condenser infers reference-token and anchor geometry to guide compression through geometry-grounded attention, improving rendering quality and enabling frustum culling during decoding. Compared with existing LVSM scene-compression baselines, GLoD-LVSM achieves the best trade-off between rendering quality and scene token count. Compared with the uncompressed base model, GLoD-LVSM reduces the scene-token count by 33.4% and accelerates rendering by $1.23\times$ with no quality loss. Under a relaxed quality-loss budget, the reduction increases to 85.5%, with $3.00\times$ rendering speedup. Further analysis reveals that view-synthesis supervision yields emergent scene depth and self-organized anchors that align with surfaces and adapt their density to local texture complexity. Beyond rendering, we further show that our scene representation also supports scene-semantic understanding, highlighting its potential for broader downstream tasks.
authors: Weikai Lin, Nicholas Milef, Carl S Marshall, Grant Kaijuin Yang, Todd Keeler, Yuhao Zhu
bullets: Addresses token redundancy that increases LVSM storage and rendering costs.
Learns a continuous field to initialize flexible numbers of scene anchors for different token budgets.
Uses an end-to-end condenser with geometry-grounded attention to guide compression and enable frustum culling during decoding.
Reduces scene tokens by 33.4% with no quality loss and provides a 1.23× rendering speedup; under relaxed quality loss, reductions reach 85.5% with 3.00× speedup.
Learned anchors self-organize along surfaces and adapt density to local texture complexity; the representation also supports scene-semantic understanding.
papers.selection_reason: Geometry-grounded continuous-LoD scene representation for large view synthesis models, reducing token count and accelerating rendering.
papers.title: GLoD-LVSM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Continuous-LoD Scene Representations for Large View Synthesis Models
papers.tldr: GLoD-LVSM compresses LVSM scene representations with continuous, geometry-grounded anchors to reduce tokens and accelerate novel-view rendering while preserving quality.

papers.abstract: Recent video world models have increasingly adopted 3D memory mechanisms to integrate historical observations into a lightweight and persistent scene representation. This naturally raises a complementary question: if 3D representations can serve as an effective mechanism for memorizing observed scenes, can they also be directly used as the latent space for reconstructing and generating scenes? Motivated by this idea, we represent a scene as a compact and unstructured 3D-anchored latent space (\textbf{SceneAE}). Each latent combines an explicit 3D position with an implicit content feature and is spatially grounded to describe its local scene region, forming a sparse latent point cloud. Unlike conventional video-VAE latents that describe how a scene appears from particular viewpoints, our representation directly describes the scene itself, making it naturally applicable to both reconstruction and generation. For reconstruction, once the scene has been generated, our persistent 3D representation can be projected and decoded into RGB-D observations by different target cameras, without the need to regenerate a video for each new camera trajectory. For generation, we leverage the geometry-content separation to first generate camera-controlled 3D geometry and then synthesize content conditioned on it, reducing camera-appearance entanglement and improving camera controllability. Experiments show that this 3D latent achieves superior generation quality, computational cost, and camera controllability.
authors: Shuofeng Sun, Wenzhao Zheng, Yunpeng Zhang, Yi Wu, Linqing Zhao, Haibin Yan
bullets: Addresses whether 3D memory representations can serve directly as latent spaces for scene reconstruction and generation.
Represents each scene with spatially grounded 3D positions plus implicit content features, forming a sparse latent point cloud.
Projects the persistent representation into RGB-D views from new cameras without regenerating videos for each trajectory.
Separates geometry generation from content synthesis to reduce camera–appearance entanglement and improve camera control.
Experiments report improved generation quality, computational cost, and camera controllability.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a 3D-anchored latent space for scene generation and reconstruction, fitting World Models (interactive generation) and 3D Vision.
papers.title: SceneAE: Scene Generation and Reconstruction in Queryable 3D-Anchored Latent Space
papers.tldr: SceneAE represents scenes as sparse, queryable 3D-anchored latents that support both camera-flexible reconstruction and controllable generation.

papers.abstract: Single-image 3D reconstruction has advanced rapidly, yet standalone garments remain challenging due to thin-shell geometry, open boundaries, and layered structures. Existing datasets and evaluation protocols provide limited support for systematic evaluation in this setting. We introduce MagicGarment, a benchmark for single-image standalone 3D garment reconstruction with 1,518 professionally constructed assets across 17 composite garment types, aligned multimodal annotations, and a unified evaluation protocol. We further establish a garment-aware reference baseline by adapting a pretrained image-to-3D backbone at two levels: Grounded Semantic Refinement (GSR) provides garment-focused visual conditioning, while Flow-Time-Route LoRA (FTR-LoRA) adapts the frozen 3D generative backbone using flow-timestep, token-routing, and expert-load information. Experiments demonstrate MagicGarment's benchmark utility and the effectiveness of garment-aware adaptation. Project page: https://1019538157.github.io/MagicGarment/.
authors: Jia Chen, Ruyang Zhao, Jun Bai, Chao Huang, Saishang Zhong, Xinrong Hu
bullets: Addresses challenges from thin-shell geometry, open boundaries, and layered garment structures.
Provides 1,518 professionally constructed assets spanning 17 composite garment types.
Includes aligned multimodal annotations and a unified evaluation protocol.
Adapts a pretrained image-to-3D model with garment-focused visual conditioning and flow-aware LoRA refinement.
Experiments show the benchmark is useful and the garment-aware adaptation is effective.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a benchmark and adaptation method for single-image 3D garment reconstruction using a pretrained backbone, fitting 3D Vision and 3D Foundation Models.
papers.title: MagicGarment: Benchmarking Single-Image Standalone 3D Garment Reconstruction
papers.tldr: MagicGarment introduces a benchmark and garment-aware baseline for evaluating single-image 3D reconstruction of standalone garments.

papers.abstract: Real measurements are too limited to train an accurate indoor pathloss predictor that works across a wide range of buildings. Large-scale synthetic pretraining offers a way forward, but real building layouts are also scarce, and accurate ray-tracing simulators are slow, expensive, and often proprietary. We address both problems by introducing a generator that automatically creates diverse indoor layouts and a fast, open-source approximate ray tracer that computes radio maps for them. Using this pipeline, we generate 128M synthetic samples, pretrain ResNet-101 and Swin-T encoder-decoders, and fine-tune them on high-quality benchmark data. Despite simulator mismatch, our ResNet-101 model reduces error by 15% on average relative to the best known methods across five indoor radio-map prediction tasks and improves transfer on a small real-measurement dataset. Both architectures show predictable data-scaling trends: power laws fitted on 2M-16M samples predict the mean normalized downstream RMSE at 32M-128M with 3.33% mean absolute percentage error for ResNet-101 and 7.10% for Swin-T. These results show that pretraining on large amounts of cheap simulated data can improve indoor radio-map prediction, even when real measurements and high-quality simulations are limited.
authors: Khoren Petrosyan, Artashes Mkrtchyan, Rafayel Mkrtchyan, Hrant Khachatrian, Theofanis P. Raptis
bullets: Addresses scarce real measurements, building layouts, and costly proprietary ray tracing.
Introduces an automatic indoor-layout generator and a fast open-source approximate ray tracer.
Pretrains ResNet-101 and Swin-T encoder-decoders on 128M synthetic samples, then fine-tunes on benchmark data.
ResNet-101 reduces error by 15% on average across five tasks and improves transfer to a small real-measurement dataset.
Scaling trends follow predictable power laws, with downstream RMSE forecasts remaining reasonably accurate at larger data scales.
papers.selection_reason: Uses synthetic 3D indoor layouts and ray tracing to pretrain models for radio-map prediction, demonstrating a transferable pipeline for 3D spatial understanding and foundation model pretraining.
papers.title: Scaling Cheap Synthetic Pretraining Improves Indoor Radio-Map Prediction
papers.tldr: Large-scale pretraining on cheaply generated synthetic indoor radio maps substantially improves prediction despite imperfect simulation fidelity.

papers.abstract: 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts. We present LLM2R, which casts part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM): a Point-BERT encoder and a Q-Former compress each part into a block of geometric tokens, the blocks of all parts are concatenated, and a causal LLM adapted with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) processes the sequence in one forward pass. Causal attention, however, lets the hidden states of a part observe only the parts that precede it. LLM2R therefore appends a block of learnable summary tokens after the last part: these tokens follow every part, so their states aggregate the whole assembly at a constant token cost, and a part-aware pose head fuses each part's states with them before predicting its rotation and translation. One architecture thus handles semantic and geometric assembly and predicts all poses in a single non-autoregressive pass. LLM2R achieves the highest part accuracy and success rate on all three PartNet categories, the best rotation error, translation error, and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the lowest translation error and fastest inference on Breaking Bad, where only a fracture-specialized method is more accurate. Its advantage grows with the number of parts: at 100 parts it exceeds GARF by 33.5 points in part accuracy on Breaking Bad and Assembler by 29.1 points on PartNet, and it transfers zero-shot to unseen categories with more than 16 points higher part accuracy than the strongest of three baselines.
authors: Zhouhan Zhong, Qiuhong Shen, Xingyi Yang, Jinyi Xu, Xinchao Wang
bullets: Problem: Pairwise and iterative assembly methods struggle as the number of parts grows because placement depends on the full set.
Method: Point-BERT and a Q-Former encode each part into geometric-token blocks, which a LoRA-adapted causal LLM processes in one pass.
Key design: Learnable summary tokens aggregate information from all parts and are fused with each part’s states to predict rotation and translation.
Results: LLM2R achieves leading or competitive accuracy, pose errors, success rate, and inference speed across PartNet, PartNeXt, and Breaking Bad.
Scope: It transfers zero-shot to unseen categories and its advantage increases for assemblies with many parts.
papers.selection_reason: LLM-based 3D part assembly with geometric token sequence modeling; relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial reasoning.
papers.title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
papers.tldr: LLM2R reframes 3D part assembly as one-pass sequence modeling with an LLM, enabling scalable prediction of all part poses using global assembly context.

papers.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) are shaped by the spectral structure induced by their input encodings and activation functions. Existing methods improve fitting primarily by modifying which frequencies are available to the network, through coordinate encodings or periodic nonlinearities. However, frequency access is not the only bottleneck: signals with localized or spatially varying structure require the network to efficiently compose frequencies into multi-harmonic internal responses. We introduce learnable spectral activations (LSA), which replace fixed neuron-level nonlinearities with a residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training. LSA does not expand the asymptotic function class. Instead, it changes the factorization of the representation: linear weights select features while activation coefficients control spectral shaping, and the two are updated by separate gradients. Because the activation output is affine in the coefficients given fixed pre-activations, spectral tuning becomes a more direct subproblem compared to architectures where it is entangled with feature selection. Empirically, this factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in the leading eigenmodes of the neural tangent kernel, consistent with improved optimization behavior. Across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks, LSA also improves reconstruction quality.
bullets: Problem: Existing encodings and periodic activations expand frequency access but may struggle with localized or spatially varying structures requiring multi-harmonic composition.
Method: Replace fixed activations with residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training.
Key idea: Linear weights select features while activation coefficients independently control spectral shaping, without expanding the asymptotic function class.

Result: The factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in leading neural tangent kernel eigenmodes and improves reconstruction quality across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces learnable spectral activations for implicit neural representations, relevant to 3D vision and efficient representation learning.
papers.title: Learnable Spectral Activations
papers.tldr: Learnable Spectral Activations improve implicit neural representations by learning how neurons compose frequencies, enabling better optimization and reconstruction across several signal domains.

papers.abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly capable of generating complex 3D structures, with the potential to reshape how objects are designed and realized in the physical world. Yet, producing elegant geometry is fundamentally different from producing objects that can be built and perform their intended functions. Existing evaluations largely focus on geometric quality while overlooking physical realizability. We introduce LMBuild, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on generating buildable and functional structures. LMBuild represents generated objects as assembled structures comprising part decompositions, joints, materials, and sequences. To support reproducible evaluation, we provide a unified framework consisting of: (1) an interactive environment in which agents can use tools to retrieve, create, and place components to construct objects; (2) a curated benchmark that repurposes established CAD datasets and augments them with knowledge from Wikipedia; and (3) a evaluation framework covering structural soundness, functional affordance, design quality, and physical realization. Evaluations across 30 systems reveal several intriguing findings: (a) Soundness and alignment are no longer the primary bottlenecks for frontier closed-source models, while functional affordance and physical operability remain substantially more challenging; (b) stronger models more effectively create new components, whereas weaker models tend to rely on retrieval; and (c) providing functional specifications substantially improves part completeness, kinematics, and physical operability. These results show that generating real-world structures requires deeper reasoning about functional affordances, mechanics, and designing and creating novel components. We expect LMBuild to provide a foundation for measuring progress and incentivizing research toward agents that generate buildable and functional structures.
bullets: Evaluates assembled structures defined by parts, joints, materials, and construction sequences.
Provides an interactive tool-use environment, a CAD- and Wikipedia-enhanced benchmark, and metrics for soundness, function, design quality, and physical realization.
Across 30 systems, functional affordance and physical operability remain harder than structural soundness and alignment for frontier closed-source models.
Stronger models create novel components more effectively, while weaker models rely more on retrieving existing components.
Functional specifications improve part completeness, kinematics, and physical operability.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a benchmark for LLM agents generating 3D structures, relevant to 3D vision and foundation models.
papers.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures
papers.tldr: LMBuild benchmarks LLM agents on generating 3D structures that are not only geometrically sound but also buildable and functionally operable.

papers.abstract: Self-supervised pretraining has expanded the pool of 3D medical foundation models, but published evaluations use different datasets, endpoints and fine-tuning protocols. Models also differ in architecture, pretraining objective and data, while downstream targets range from voxel-level masks to patient-level diagnoses and outcomes. As a result, published findings provide little directly comparable evidence for choosing a model for a new task. Direct comparison of adaptation performance requires fine-tuning candidates on labelled target data, at substantial computational cost. We benchmark 23 candidates across the same 14 segmentation, classification and regression tasks spanning multiple anatomies and modalities. No candidate ranked among the top three across all segmentation tasks or across all classification and regression tasks; a convolutional encoder could outperform a transformer trained with the same objective on one task but underperform it on another. We benchmark transferability estimators against the fine-tuned rankings and find that their agreement varies across dense segmentation, classification and regression. InsightRank uses task-appropriate frozen-feature statistics and architecture-aware pairwise comparisons to rank candidates before fine-tuning. Across the 23-model pool, mean Kendall tau-b was 0.431 for segmentation and 0.352 for classification and regression. The segmentation Top 3 contained a task winner on four of nine tasks; the image-level Top 3 contained none on the five tasks, despite better full-ranking agreement than the matched conventional estimators. A three-model shortlist reduced recorded extraction-plus-training job time by 85.8% across seven segmentation tasks. Together, the benchmark provides a common reference for model selection and InsightRank offers a lower-cost way to prioritize fine-tuning, with shortlist performance that differs by target type.
authors: Jiaqi Tang, Yu Wang, Yang Liu, Jing Tao, Fandong Zhang, Zhou Zhen, Xiahai Zhuang, Qingchao Chen, Yining Yang, Yizhou Yu
bullets: Models were evaluated consistently across 14 segmentation, classification, and regression tasks covering multiple anatomies and modalities.
No model ranked among the top three across all tasks; architecture advantages varied by task.
Transferability estimators agreed with fine-tuned rankings differently for segmentation versus image-level prediction tasks.
InsightRank uses task-specific frozen-feature statistics and architecture-aware comparisons to rank models before fine-tuning.
A three-model shortlist reduced recorded extraction-plus-training job time by 85.8% across seven segmentation tasks, but shortlist effectiveness varied by target type.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmarks and ranks self-supervised 3D medical vision foundation models, fitting 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Benchmarking Self-Supervised 3D Medical Vision Foundation Models and Transferability Estimation
papers.tldr: A benchmark of 23 self-supervised 3D medical vision models shows that transferability is highly task-dependent, while InsightRank can reduce fine-tuning costs by prioritizing candidates.

papers.abstract: Modeling 3D hair strands is challenging due to complex hairstyle geometry, scarce high-quality training data, and incomplete or noisy input observations. Foundation models offer broader hairstyle priors, but their outputs are not directly usable for strand-based rendering and simulation. Existing approaches require costly per-instance optimization to fit hair priors to meshes from foundation models and 2D orientations from specialized predictors trained on limited hair data, restricting efficiency and generalization. We present HairFlow, a multimodal conditioned diffusion framework for efficient and controllable hair strands modeling. HairFlow conditions strand generation on two complementary representations: a coarse mesh that constrains global shape and multi-view sketches that specify local strand flow. HairFlow combines an Orientation VAE with a conditioned diffusion transformer to generate volumetric fields that are traced into explicit strands. To overcome the lack of paired sketch-strand training data, we introduce an automatic synthesis pipeline that generates geometrically aligned multi-view sketches with diverse styles representative of inference-time inputs. Experiments show that HairFlow generates plausible 3D strands that faithfully follow the input conditions across diverse hairstyles, substantially reduces inference time, and supports flexible multimodal control.
authors: Yating Wang, Kui Wu, Ran Yi, Zixuan Lu, Tongtong Wang, Zhongtian Zheng, Lizhuang Ma, Yuefan Shen
bullets: Addresses complex hair geometry, limited training data, and noisy or incomplete observations.
Uses a coarse mesh for global hairstyle shape and multi-view sketches for local strand flow.
Combines an Orientation VAE with a conditioned diffusion transformer to produce volumetric fields traced into explicit strands.
Introduces automatic synthesis of aligned, stylistically diverse sketch–strand training pairs.
Experiments show plausible strands that follow inputs across diverse hairstyles, with reduced inference time and flexible multimodal control.
papers.selection_reason: Presents HairFlow, a multimodal conditioned diffusion framework for generating 3D hair strands, contributing to 3D foundation models and generative 3D geometry.
papers.title: HairFlow: Modeling 3D Hair Strands with Multi-Modal Conditioned Diffusion
papers.tldr: HairFlow efficiently generates controllable 3D hair strands from coarse meshes and multi-view sketches using conditioned diffusion.

papers.abstract: Generating accurate 3D molecules requires jointly determining a variable number of atoms, their identities, and geometry across spatial scales: global shape emerges coarsely, whereas chemical bonds demand fine local precision. Existing atom-based diffusion and flow models operate largely at a single scale, while dense spatial fields become costly at high resolution. We introduce OctMole, a multiscale octree flow framework for 3D molecular generation. A hierarchical occupancy flow progressively resolves sparse molecular support from coarse to fine, and a joint atom flow assigns atom types and continuous in-cell offsets to occupied leaves. This decomposition combines efficient global structure with subcell geometric precision, while cell corruption improves robustness to generated support. On QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, OctMole achieves strong chemical, distributional, and geometric quality, with particularly clear gains over Uni-3DAR on GEOM-DRUG and substantial efficiency gains over dense 3D generation. As an additional capability, intermediate occupancy states and selected regions provide spatial conditioning without task-specific retraining, supporting multiscale shape conditioning, regional editing, linker generation, and shape interpolation. Code and pretrained checkpoints are available at https://github.com/octree-nn/octmole and https://huggingface.co/Disembo/octmole, respectively.
authors: Yu-Tong Jin, Yi-Yang Tian, Qiwei Ye, Peng-Shuai Wang
bullets: Models sparse molecular structure from coarse global shape to fine local geometry.
Uses a hierarchical occupancy flow plus a joint atom flow for atom identities and in-cell offsets.
Cell corruption improves robustness to generated molecular support.
Shows strong chemical, distributional, and geometric quality on QM9 and GEOM-DRUG, with efficiency gains over dense 3D generation.
Enables spatial conditioning for shape control, regional editing, linker generation, and shape interpolation without task-specific retraining.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces OctMole, a multiscale octree flow framework for 3D molecular generation. The hierarchical spatial flow approach is a transferable technique for 3D generation tasks.
papers.title: OctMole: Multiscale 3D Molecular Generation with Hierarchical Spatial Flows
papers.tldr: OctMole generates 3D molecules efficiently by combining hierarchical octree structure modeling with fine-grained atom placement and typing.

papers.abstract: We present Unravel, a training-free framework that turns a single image into an interactive 3D scene, where every object is an independent and movable asset. Existing generators either produce one entangled geometry in which no object can be moved, or predict all objects in one feed-forward pass, where a wrong guess cannot be detected or repaired. Unravel instead takes a different approach: it first takes the scene apart, and then puts it back together. Starting from the input image, an agentic harness that iteratively peels the image layer by layer, and adopts point cloud as major modality for spatial relationship recovery. Specifically, a vision-language model plans which objects are fully visible, an image editor removes them and restores the occluded regions. Every edit is verified before being incorporated into the reconstruction. This process gradually turns occluded parts of the scene into direct observation, allowing objects to be reconstructed when they are best exposed rather than hallucinated from the original image alone. The scene is then rebuilt in reverse removal order, so that the supporting objects are naturally placed before the objects they support. Since a single-view image only reveals part of an object, we treat the observed points as a lower bound on its size: an asset may grow to cover its points, but can not shrink away from them. Finally, we physically settle the reconstructed scene to remove floating objects and interpenetrations, followed by an agentic audit that corrects remaining placement errors. Extensive experiments on diverse indoor scenes show that Unravel recovers more objects, places them more faithfully, and produces scenes that are more physically-plausible than existing methods.
authors: Hui Shan, Keyang Luo, Binjia Zhou, Ming Li, Kai Li, Xin Wang, Zhenyang Li, Zesong Yang, Weikai Chen, Runze Zhang, Xin Wang, Yanwei Fu, Zhen Chen, Xiangru Huang
bullets: Targets the limitations of entangled scene generators and one-shot object prediction, where objects cannot be moved or errors are difficult to fix.
Uses a training-free agentic process: a vision-language model selects visible objects, an image editor removes them and restores occlusions, and each edit is verified.
Represents spatial relationships with point clouds and reconstructs objects in reverse removal order to preserve support relationships.
Treats visible points as a minimum object extent, then physically settles the scene and audits placements to reduce floating and intersecting objects.
Experiments on diverse indoor scenes report more complete object recovery, more faithful placement, and greater physical plausibility than existing methods.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a framework for recovering interactive 3D scenes from a single image using point clouds and VLMs. This falls squarely under 3D perception and scene reconstruction.
papers.title: Unravel: Recovering an Interactive 3D Scene from a Single Image
papers.tldr: Unravel reconstructs a single image into an editable, physically plausible 3D scene by iteratively separating, repairing, and reassembling objects.

papers.abstract: High-fidelity closed-loop simulation for autonomous driving increasingly relies on dense multi-view 3D reconstruction. While recent feed-forward geometric foundation models have revolutionized per-scene optimization, applying them to continuous, long-horizon driving sequences is computationally intractable due to GPU memory limits and the quadratic complexity of global attention. Existing scaling strategies are fundamentally limited, as causal streaming suffers from compounding scale drift and trajectory deviation, while rigid "chunk-then-align" heuristics fragment global context and produce trajectory discontinuities. To address these limitations, we introduce Drive3R, a block-wise streaming geometric foundation model. Its block-wise causal attention resolves the scalability bottleneck of fully bidirectional attention while avoiding the loss of local future context in purely causal streaming. Its confidence-aware re-anchoring further mitigates long-range drift by detecting unreliable streaming states, re-initializing the KV cache, and stitching refreshed segments through SE(3) alignment. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Drive3R establishes a new state-of-the-art on nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo. Specifically, on nuScenes, it improves over the recent DVGT-2 baseline from 0.1806 to 0.1081 in AbsRel, from 0.6750 to 0.5344 in point-cloud Accuracy, and from 1.5812 to 0.9092 in ATE.
authors: Tianyi Yang, Haojun Yang, Jipeng Xiao, Xuesong Chen, Shaoshuai Shi, Li Jiang, Zhipeng Zhang
bullets: Addresses GPU-memory and quadratic-attention limits in continuous multi-view 3D reconstruction.
Uses block-wise causal attention to retain local future context while scaling beyond full bidirectional attention.
Detects unreliable streaming states, re-initializes the KV cache, and stitches refreshed segments with SE(3) alignment to reduce drift and trajectory discontinuities.
Achieves state-of-the-art results on nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo; on nuScenes, it improves AbsRel, point-cloud Accuracy, and ATE over DVGT-2.
papers.selection_reason: Streaming geometric foundation model for multi-view 3D reconstruction, with block-wise attention and KV cache re-anchoring for long-horizon driving.
papers.title: Drive3R: Block-wise Streaming Geometric Foundation Models for Autonomous Driving
papers.tldr: Drive3R enables scalable, drift-resistant 3D reconstruction for long-horizon autonomous-driving sequences through block-wise streaming attention and confidence-aware re-anchoring.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward geometric foundation models (GFMs) directly predict dense geometry and camera poses from batches of images. Emerging visual SLAM methods chain together consecutive GFM batches to form dense point cloud maps. A core challenge is how to address the ambiguous geometric scale of GFM predictions: independent predictions are locally consistent up-to-scale but not constrained by any direct physical measurements. Models trained on data with known scale improve the consistency of GFM reconstructions but again do not directly measure it. Consequently, trajectories and 3D reconstructions from GFM-enabled SLAM methods inherit this issue. Motivated by parallels with classical visual-inertial odometry, we introduce FoundationVIO which integrates inertial sensing with GFM predictions to recover metric scale reconstruction using a factor-graph based approach. We demonstrate odometry estimates competitive with classical state-of-the-art VIO methods and accurate dense reconstructions that outperform GFM-enabled SLAM methods. We also add a minimal GFM-based loop-closure mechanism to create a full Visual-Inertial SLAM system capable of creating globally accurate reconstructions and pose estimates. We evaluate our method on three datasets with well known sensor systems and demonstrate its compatibility on ubiquitous camera and IMU sensors. The method runs at approximately real-time on a consumer-grade laptop GPU. Code: https://github.com/ori-drs/FoundationVIO.
authors: Jin Rhee, Yuhao Zhang, Frank Dellaert, Maurice Fallon
bullets: Addresses the scale ambiguity inherited by feed-forward geometric foundation models and GFM-based SLAM.
Uses a factor-graph approach to integrate inertial sensing with GFM geometry and camera-pose predictions.
Achieves odometry competitive with classical state-of-the-art VIO and denser reconstructions than GFM-based SLAM methods.
Adds a minimal GFM-based loop-closure mechanism for globally accurate visual-inertial SLAM.
Evaluated on three datasets with common camera/IMU systems and runs approximately in real time on a consumer laptop GPU.
papers.selection_reason: Integrates geometric foundation model predictions with inertial sensing for metric-scale VIO/SLAM; relevant to 3D perception and foundation-model-based geometry.
papers.title: FoundationVIO: Enforcing Metric Scale in Feed-forward Visual-Inertial Odometry
papers.tldr: FoundationVIO combines geometric foundation-model predictions with IMU measurements to recover metric-scale visual-inertial odometry and dense SLAM reconstructions.

papers.abstract: Purpose : To develop and evaluate CAPTOR, a deep-learning vision-language foundation model for oncologic chest-abdomen-pelvis (CAP) CT interpretation. Materials & Methods : CAPTOR (Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis foundaTion model for Oncologic Radiology) is a contrastive vision-language model, trained using a pretraining strategy for oncologic CAP CT (in single- or multiple-series acquisitions), on a multicenter retrospective dataset from North America, Europe and Asia, predominantly from tumor lesion examinations. CAPTOR was compared with state-of-the-art CT foundation models on three downstream tasks: disease detection, survival prediction using TumorImagingBench and image retrieval. Classification and retrieval were both evaluated on held-out internal and public test sets, stratified by anatomical coverage and indication. Bootstrap resampling was used to estimate confidence intervals, and pairwise comparisons were performed using permutation tests. Results : CAPTOR was trained and tested on 25,512 and 10,794 CT-report pairs respectively. TumorImagingBench datasets comprised between 134 and 421 studies each. CAPTOR outperformed all baseline models, on the classification task, on the CAP subset (AUC 0.767, 95%CI: 0.734-0.793, vs. 0.695, 95%CI: 0.645-0.736 for the next-best, p<0.001) and oncologic subset (AUC 0.784, 95%CI: 0.759-0.805, vs. 0.734, 95%CI: 0.703-0.767 p<0.001), ranked first on three of the four oncologic prognostic benchmarks, and achieved superior retrieval performance on CAP and oncologic subsets. Conclusion : A foundation model trained on oncology-enriched CAP CT data outperformed relevant state-of-the-art models in its target clinical context, underscoring the importance of clinically aligned pretraining. We release our preprocessing, training and inference code : https://github.com/Guerbet-AI/CAPTOR and model weights : https://huggingface.co/Guerbet-AI/CAPTOR
authors: S\'el\'ena Jean-Mactoux, Sophie Loizillon, Ghina Jardali, Amandine Cromb\'e, Nathalie Lassau, Alexandre B\^one
bullets: Uses contrastive vision-language pretraining on multicenter oncologic CAP CT-report pairs, including single- and multiple-series acquisitions.
Evaluated for disease detection, survival prediction, and image retrieval across internal and public test sets.
Achieved the best classification performance on CAP and oncologic subsets, and ranked first on three of four prognostic benchmarks.
Showed superior image retrieval performance on CAP and oncologic subsets.
Preprocessing, training, inference code, and model weights are publicly released.
papers.selection_reason: Vision-language foundation model for 3D oncologic CT, fits multimodal and 3D foundation model interests.
papers.title: CAPTOR: a vision-language foundation model for Chest-Abdomen-Pelvis Oncologic CT
papers.tldr: CAPTOR is an oncology-focused vision-language foundation model for chest-abdomen-pelvis CT that outperformed existing CT foundation models across detection, prognosis, and retrieval tasks.

papers.abstract: Image-level MRI harmonization is often evaluated with a frozen site probe, a site classifier trained on raw scans and applied unchanged to harmonized ones: a drop in its accuracy is read as removal of site effects. We audit this practice on ABIDE I (1,112 T1-weighted scans, 17 sites) with ten output sets from seven harmonization methods and controls for chance, head shape, intensity, preprocessing and target alignment. We find that this verdict depends on how the probe is trained, even among probes that classify raw scans well: across random seeds, its balanced accuracy on the same CycleGAN outputs ranges from 0.13 to 0.59 (chance: 0.06). Low frozen-probe accuracy can also arise without harmonization: a Gaussian blur, which increases the intensity distance to the target site, lowers this accuracy to chance. Moreover, where the frozen probe fails, probes trained on the harmonized scans still recover the site, even from intensity histograms alone: on HACA3 outputs, the frozen probe scores 0.25, a probe trained on those outputs 0.75, and one using only their intensity histograms 0.71. Low frozen-probe accuracy therefore does not show that site information has been removed. We recommend reporting several probes trained to convergence, probes trained on harmonized scans, and target alignment.
authors: Muhammad Muqsit Islam, Gloria Garc\'ia Cuenco, Jos\'e M. Mart\'inez, Pierrick Coup\'e
bullets: The audit examines ten harmonized output sets from seven methods on ABIDE I MRI scans, with controls for chance, image properties, preprocessing, and target alignment.
Frozen-probe balanced accuracy varies widely across random seeds on identical outputs, despite strong raw-scan classification performance.
Non-harmonizing changes such as Gaussian blur can reduce frozen-probe accuracy to chance while increasing mismatch with the target site.
Site information can remain recoverable from harmonized scans, including from intensity histograms, even when the frozen probe performs poorly.
The authors recommend multiple converged probes, probes retrained on harmonized outputs, and explicit target-alignment reporting.
papers.selection_reason: Audits evaluation practices for multi-site MRI harmonization, highlighting the limitations of frozen site probes and proposing better metrics for adaptation across sites.
papers.title: Frozen Site-Probe Accuracy Is Not a Standalone Harmonization Score: An Audit of Evaluation Practice for Multi-Site MRI
papers.tldr: Frozen site-probe accuracy is an unreliable standalone measure of MRI harmonization because low scores can reflect probe instability or image degradation rather than removal of site information.

papers.abstract: Sparse-view cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) is severely under-constrained by limited X-ray projections. Learned reconstruction can provide complementary anatomical information, but using it as a prior in patient-specific Gaussian reconstruction introduces two challenges. First, the discrepancy between the learned prior and current reconstruction is spatially non-uniform: some local differences contain useful missing 3D information, whereas others reflect prior bias. Second, even a volumetrically beneficial correction can conflict with the observed X-ray measurements. Since X-ray measurements are line integrals, spatially separated corrections may affect overlapping rays, with their signed projection responses reinforcing or partially canceling in the measurement residual, so their feasibility cannot always be assessed independently. In this paper, we introduce RePrior, a multi-stage progressive prior-correction framework that addresses correction actionability, measurement feasibility, and representation expressivity. Selective Correction Proposal (SCP) first identifies actionable signed local corrections from prior--reconstruction discrepancies. Measurement-Constrained Reconciliation (MCR) then jointly enforces their consistency with patient-specific X-ray measurements, while Hybrid Residual Enhancement (HRE) recovers additional correction capacity through complementary voxel- and Gaussian-domain degrees of freedom around the reconciled anchor. RePrior requires neither test-time ground truth nor case-specific network fine-tuning. RePrior gains approximately 2.6~dB in 3D PSNR over R$^2$-Gaussian across LUNA16, PANORAMA, and PENGWIN. Beyond prior-assisted reconstruction, it delivers additional gains in volumetric quality and observed-view projection fidelity, with consistent gains in held-out-view fidelity in the backbone-matched evaluation.
authors: Mengrui Yin, Tianxingjian Ding, Wufan Zhao, Ziyang Yan, Yu Tian
bullets: Addresses spatially varying prior bias and conflicts between volumetric corrections and overlapping-ray measurements.
Uses three stages: Selective Correction Proposal, Measurement-Constrained Reconciliation, and Hybrid Residual Enhancement.
Requires neither test-time ground truth nor case-specific network fine-tuning.
Reports approximately 2.6 dB higher 3D PSNR than R²-Gaussian across LUNA16, PANORAMA, and PENGWIN.
Also improves volumetric quality, observed-view projection fidelity, and—under backbone-matched evaluation—held-out-view fidelity.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses sparse-view CBCT reconstruction using a learned prior correction framework (RePrior) that reconciles measurement constraints with volumetric reconstruction, applicable to general 3D reconstruction.
papers.title: RePrior: Measurement-Reconciled Prior Correction for Sparse-View CBCT Reconstruction
papers.tldr: RePrior improves sparse-view CBCT reconstruction by selectively correcting learned-prior errors while enforcing consistency with patient-specific X-ray measurements.

papers.abstract: A central challenge in de novo protein design is generating proteins with desired structural and functional properties. Existing design models typically require a dedicated input representation for each property, limiting the design objectives they support. We develop Prompteina, the first all-atom structure generation model that supports new and broader design objectives specified in natural language, analogous to text-to-image generation. To train Prompteina, we construct Prompteina-Data, a paired text--protein structure dataset of 1.8M structures and 50M+ captions describing global and residue-specific structural and functional properties. We adapt Proteina-Complexa, a pretrained structure generation model, through text-conditioned pretraining and finetuning that aligns residues with their corresponding text. Prompteina outperforms baselines on 15 of 18 structural properties and generates proteins that more closely match descriptions of their intended functions. In binder design, it leads baselines on at least 13 of 20 targets and improves interface confidence by 14\% over the strongest baseline. With iterative in silico feedback, Prompteina's gain over non-iterative generation is 57\% larger than the next-best baseline on the hardest targets. Finally, we experimentally validate Prompteina designs against GM2A, a target with no reported de novo binders. We identify nine binders, with the strongest at an apparent $K_{\mathrm{D}}$ of 107 nM. These results establish natural language as an effective and powerful conditioning interface for protein structure generation.
authors: Joseph Lee, Yanjing Li, Bo Qiang, Gregory Lau, Allyson Ettinger, Noah A. Smith, Rory Donovan-Maiye, David Baker, Hanna Hajishirzi, Pang Wei Koh
bullets: Addresses the limited range of objectives supported by protein design models requiring property-specific input representations.
Introduces Prompteina, an all-atom structure generator conditioned on natural-language descriptions of global and residue-specific properties.
Trains on Prompteina-Data, containing 1.8M protein structures and over 50M paired captions, with text–residue alignment.
Outperforms baselines on 15 of 18 structural properties and leads on at least 13 of 20 binder-design targets; iterative feedback further improves performance.
Experimental validation against GM2A identified nine binders, with the strongest showing an apparent KD of 107 nM.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a text-conditioned all-atom 3D structure generation foundation model, directly fitting multimodal foundation models and 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Designing Protein Structures from Natural Language
papers.tldr: Prompteina enables natural-language-guided generation of protein structures and produces designs that better satisfy structural and functional goals, including experimentally validated binders.

papers.abstract: Multi-view representations enable pretrained image and video vision-language models to understand 3D scenes, but their long visual token sequences make inference costly. Redundancy arises both from repeated observations of the same scene regions across views and from processing all visual tokens at every LLM layer, regardless of their relevance to the current computation. We propose GeoGR, a two-stage framework that jointly compresses scene representations and visual computation. At the projector level, GeoSemZip consolidates cross-view observations into 3D voxel tokens and combines semantic saliency with spatial coverage to construct a compact scene representation. Unselected voxel features are aggregated into contextual anchors to retain scene information that would otherwise be discarded. At the LLM level, we identify an effective visual computation window and observe that query-conditioned token relevance remains locally stable but changes over longer layer intervals. Guided by these findings, GroupRoute combines late entry and early exit with recoverable group-wise skipping. Low-relevance tokens bypass complete LLM layers while retaining their hidden states and can rejoin the active group at subsequent anchor layers selected under a computation budget. For compression-aware post-training, we construct a compact dataset of 67K samples by retaining 30% of the original training pool. With this protocol, GeoGR retains 95.2% and 96.8% of the dense post-trained models' performance on LLaVA-OneVision-7B and Video-3D LLM-7B, respectively, while accelerating LLM prefill by $6.8\times$ and $6.1\times$. These results demonstrate the consistent effectiveness of GeoGR across 3D VLMs with and without explicit 3D spatial encoding, highlighting a favorable performance-efficiency trade-off. The code is available at https://github.com/EIT-NLP/GeoGR.
authors: Yongxin Zheng, Hao Wu, Fang Li, Hu Fu, Peiran Yin, Xudong Wang, Haozhe Hu, Xinghao Chen, Yunpu Ma, Wei Zhang, Xiaoyu Shen
bullets: Addresses high inference cost from repeated cross-view observations and processing all visual tokens at every LLM layer.
GeoSemZip builds compact 3D voxel-token representations using semantic saliency and spatial coverage, while retaining discarded information in contextual anchors.
GroupRoute uses late entry, early exit, and recoverable group-wise skipping to adapt visual computation to token relevance.
Using a 67K-sample compression-aware post-training set, GeoGR retains 95.2% and 96.8% of dense-model performance on two 7B 3D VLMs.
It accelerates LLM prefill by 6.8× and 6.1×, demonstrating applicability to models with and without explicit 3D spatial encoding.
papers.selection_reason: Compresses 3D visual tokens and skips LLM layers for efficient 3D VLMs, directly relevant to token pruning and multimodal efficiency.
papers.title: GeoGR: Spatial-Semantic Token Compression and Group Routing for Efficient 3D VLMs
papers.tldr: GeoGR makes multi-view 3D vision-language models substantially faster by compressing redundant scene tokens and selectively routing visual tokens through LLM layers while preserving most performance.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models reconstruct scenes from unposed images, but the quadratic cost of global attention limits their scalability to large view sets. We present Zebra3D, a layerwise sparse-linear hybrid attention framework that improves the efficiency of pretrained 3D foundation models without training from scratch. Across VGGT, HunyuanWorld-Mirror, and $\pi^3$, we observe a broadly consistent depth-wise pattern: early stages are relatively tolerant to linear replacement, while sensitive middle-to-late stages tend to exhibit more concentrated attention. Zebra3D exploits this structure by assigning linear-centered attention to tolerant stages and tile-sparse attention to sensitive stages, using landmark summaries to preserve unselected context. Closed-form affine fitting enables training-free conversion, while optional post-conversion training combines task supervision with output and relational feature distillation. Across all three backbones, Zebra3D achieves strong reconstruction and camera-pose accuracy at high attention sparsity, with training-free variants remaining close to their dense counterparts. End-to-end speedups increase with input view count, reaching up to $7.1\times$ at 1,024 views. After post-conversion training, Zebra3D-VGGT reaches 80.5\% RealEstate10K AUC@30 at 94\% mean attention sparsity, within 1.1 percentage points of dense VGGT fine-tuned on the same data and schedule.
authors: Utkarsh Saxena, Ruijing Yang, Mehdi Rezagholizadeh, Akash Haridas, Vikram Appia, Emad Barsoum
bullets: Addresses the quadratic cost of global attention in feed-forward 3D foundation models for unposed-image reconstruction.
Assigns linear-centered attention to tolerant early stages and tile-sparse attention with landmark summaries to sensitive middle-to-late stages.
Converts models without training from scratch using closed-form affine fitting; optional distillation-based post-conversion training further improves performance.
Across VGGT, HunyuanWorld-Mirror, and π³, maintains strong reconstruction and camera-pose accuracy at high attention sparsity.
Zebra3D-VGGT reaches 80.5% RealEstate10K AUC@30 at 94% mean sparsity, within 1.1 percentage points of dense fine-tuned VGGT; speedup reaches 7.1× at 1,024 views.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a layerwise sparse-linear hybrid attention framework to improve the scalability of 3D foundation models, directly addressing efficiency in 3D reconstruction.
papers.title: Zebra3D: Efficient Hybrid Foundation Models For Scalable 3D Reconstruction
papers.tldr: Zebra3D makes pretrained 3D reconstruction models scalable to many views by replacing dense attention with layerwise hybrid sparse-linear attention, achieving up to 7.1× speedup with limited accuracy loss.

papers.abstract: Deep learning on cortical surfaces faces a dilemma: capturing the complex topology of over 60 nomenclature-dependent sulci per hemisphere requires high-capacity models, yet the extreme scarcity of expert annotations ($N=62$ subjects) inevitably causes overfitting. Standard supervised approaches fail to generalize in this data-scarce regime, particularly for variable and small sulci where topological ambiguity is high. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a Geometric-to-Semantic Spherical Transfer Learning framework. First, we leverage massive unlabeled data (UK Biobank, $\approx$30,000 subjects) to pre-train a spherical encoder using a locally-optimized strategy. By relying solely on continuous surface features (curvature and depth), the relevance of this pre-training is confirmed by the model's ability to detect localized and rare topological traits, such as sulcal interruptions. The downstream labeling task, however, introduces extracted sulcal fundi (lines) as an explicit semantic input. To bridge this dimensional domain gap (from purely geometric to semantic) without causing catastrophic forgetting, these anatomical lines are integrated into the pre-trained backbone via a soft-initialized Topological Prior Injector. Our experiments demonstrate that this approach outperforms fully supervised baselines trained from scratch, achieving a mean Dice of 0.77.
